docs.title: lrsomatic
docs.text:
Somatic variant calling for Oxford Nanopore and PacBio long reads: alignment, small variants, structural variants, copy number and modified bases, in matched tumour–normal or tumour-only mode.

  • Usage

    Samplesheet format, profiles, references and how to run the pipeline.

  • Output

    Every output directory and file, and how to read it.

  • Parameters

    All command-line parameters, generated from the schema.

  • Changelog

    What changed in each release.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic is a robust bioinformatics pipeline designed for processing and analyzing somatic DNA sequencing data for long-read sequencing technologies from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio. It supports both canonical base DNA and modified base calling, including specialized applications such as Fiber-seq.

This end-to-end pipeline handles the entire workflow — from raw read processing and alignment, to comprehensive somatic variant calling, including single nucleotide variants, indels, structural variants, copy number alterations, and modified bases.

It can be run in both matched tumour-normal and tumour-only mode, offering flexibility depending on the users study design.

Developed using Nextflow DSL2, it offers high portability and scalability across diverse computing environments. By leveraging Docker or Singularity containers, installation is streamlined and results are highly reproducible. Each process runs in an isolated container, simplifying dependency management and updates. Where applicable, pipeline components are sourced from nf-core/modules, promoting reuse, interoperability, and consistency within the broader Nextflow and nf-core ecosystems.

docs.title: Pipeline summary
docs.text:
1) Pre-processing:

a. Raw read QC (cramino)

b. Alignment to the reference genome (minimap2)

c. Post alignment QC (cramino, samtools idxstats, samtools flagstats, samtools stats)

d. Specific for calling modified base calling (Modkit, Fibertools)

2i) Matched mode: small variant calling:

a. Calling Germline SNPs (Clair3)

b. Phasing and Haplotagging the SNPs in the normal and tumour BAM (LongPhase)

c. Calling somatic SNVs (ClairS)

d. Phasing somatic SNVs and indels from the haplotagged tumour reads (pysam)

2ii) Tumour only mode: small variant calling:

a. Calling Germline SNPs and somatic SNVs (ClairS-TO)

b. Phasing and Haplotagging germline SNPs in tumour BAM (LongPhase)

c. Phasing somatic SNVs and indels from the haplotagged tumour reads (pysam)

3) Large variant calling:

a. Somatic structural variant calling (Severus)

b. Somatic structural variant and copy-number calling (SAVANA)

c. Copy number alterion calling; long read version of (ASCAT)

4) Annotation:

a. Small variant annotation (VEP), with pathogenicity and clinical-significance plugins: AlphaMissense, ClinVar, REVEL, SIFT/PolyPhen, and optionally CADD and EVE

b. Structural variant annotation (VEP)

c. Somatic SV and CNA functional annotation (Padfoot)

5) Visualisation:

a. Rearrangement and copy-number figures per CN/SV caller pair (ReConPlot)

6) Chromothripsis:

a. Chromothripsis calls with PCAWG confidence tiers per CN/SV caller pair (ShatterSeek)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
[!NOTE] If you are new to Nextflow and nf-core, please refer to this page on how to set-up Nextflow. Make sure to test your setup with -profile test before running the workflow on actual data.

First prepare a samplesheet with your input data that looks as follows:

sample,bam_tumor,bam_normal,platform,sex,fiber
sample1,tumour.bam,normal.bam,ont,female,n
sample2,tumour.bam,,ont,female,y
sample3,tumour.bam,,pb,male,n
sample4,tumour.bam,normal.bam,pb,male,y

Each row is a sample. BAMs/CRAMs may be unaligned or aligned (every input is realigned unless --skip_alignment is set), all fields except bam_normal are required, and an empty bam_normal runs the sample in tumour-only mode. platform is ont or pb, sex is female or male, and fiber is y or n for Fiber-seq; see the usage documentation.

Now, you can run the pipeline using:

nextflow run IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic \
   -profile <docker/singularity/.../institute> \
   --input samplesheet.csv \
   --outdir <OUTDIR>

More detail is given in our usage documentation

[!WARNING] Please provide pipeline parameters via the CLI or Nextflow -params-file option. Custom config files including those provided by the -c Nextflow option can be used to provide any configuration except for parameters; see docs.

docs.title: Pipeline output
docs.text:
The main output is an aligned and phased tumour BAM, per-sample QC from cramino, mosdepth, samtools and optionally fibertools, a MultiQC report, and a self-contained per-sample HTML report (<sample>/report/<sample>_report.html; disable it with --skip_report).

docs.title: IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic: Contributing guidelines
docs.text:
Hi there! Thanks for taking an interest in improving IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic.

This page describes the recommended nf-core way to contribute to both IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic and nf-core pipelines in general, including:

  • General contribution guidelines: common procedures or guides across all nf-core pipelines.
  • Pipeline-specific contribution guidelines: procedures or guides specific to the development conventions of IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic.

docs.title: Contribution quick start
docs.text:
To contribute code to any nf-core pipeline:

  • [ ] Ensure you have Nextflow, nf-core tools, and nf-test installed. See the nf-core/tools repository for instructions.
  • [ ] Check whether a GitHub issue about your idea already exists. If an issue does not exist, create one so that others are aware you are working on it.
  • [ ] Fork the IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic repository to your GitHub account.
  • [ ] Create a branch on your forked repository and make your changes following pipeline conventions (if applicable).
  • [ ] To fix major bugs, name your branch patch and follow the patch release process.
  • [ ] Update relevant documentation within the docs/ folder, use nf-core/tools to update nextflow_schema.json, and update CITATIONS.md.
  • [ ] Run and/or update tests. See Testing for more information.
  • [ ] Lint your code with nf-core/tools.
  • [ ] Submit a pull request (PR) against the dev branch and request a review.

If you are not used to this workflow with Git, see the GitHub documentation or Git resources for more information.

docs.title: GitHub Codespaces
docs.text:
You can contribute to IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic without installing a local development environment on your machine by using GitHub Codespaces.

GitHub Codespaces is an online developer environment that runs in your browser, complete with VS Code and a terminal. Most nf-core repositories include a devcontainer configuration, which creates a GitHub Codespaces environment specifically for Nextflow development. The environment includes pre-installed nf-core tools, Nextflow, and a few other helpful utilities via a Docker container.

To get started, open the repository in Codespaces.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Once you have made your changes, run the pipeline with nf-test to test them locally. For additional information, use the --verbose flag to view the Nextflow console log output.

nf-test test --tag test --profile +docker --verbose

If you have added new functionality, ensure you update the test assertions in the .nf.test files in the tests/ directory. Update the snapshots with the following command:

nf-test test --tag test --profile +docker --verbose --update-snapshots

When you create a pull request with changes, GitHub Actions will run automatic tests. Pull requests are typically reviewed when these tests are passing.

Two types of tests are typically run:

docs.title: Lint tests
docs.text:
nf-core has a set of guidelines which all pipelines must follow. To enforce these, run linting with nf-core/tools:

nf-core pipelines lint <pipeline_directory>

If you encounter failures or warnings, follow the linked documentation printed to screen. For more information about linting tests, see nf-core/tools API documentation.

docs.title: Pipeline tests
docs.text: Each nf-core pipeline should be set up with a minimal set of test data. GitHub Actions runs the pipeline on this data to ensure it runs through and exits successfully. If there are any failures then the automated tests fail. These tests are run with the latest available version of Nextflow and the minimum required version specified in the pipeline code.

docs.title: Patch release
docs.text:
[!WARNING] Only in the unlikely event of a release that contains a critical bug.

  • [ ] Create a new branch patch on your fork based on upstream/main or upstream/master.
  • [ ] Fix the bug and use nf-core/tools to bump the version to the next semantic version, for example, 1.2.3 → 1.2.4.
  • [ ] Open a Pull Request from patch directly to main/master with the changes.

docs.title: Pipeline contribution conventions
docs.text: nf-core semi-standardises how you write code and other contributions to make the IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic code and processing logic more understandable for new contributors and to ensure quality.

docs.title: Add a new pipeline step
docs.text:
To contribute a new step to the pipeline, follow the general nf-core coding procedure. Please also refer to the pipeline-specific contribution guidelines:

  • [ ] Define the corresponding input channel into your new process from the expected previous process channel.
  • [ ] Install a module with nf-core/tools, or write a local module (see default processes resource requirements), and add it to the target <workflow>.nf.
  • [ ] Define the output channel if needed. Mix the version output channel into ch_versions and relevant files into ch_multiqc.
  • [ ] Add new or updated parameters to nextflow.config with a default value.
  • [ ] Add new or updated parameters and relevant help text to nextflow_schema.json with nf-core/tools.
  • [ ] Add validation for relevant parameters to the pipeline utilisation section of utils_nfcore_\_pipeline/main.nf subworkflow.
  • [ ] Perform local tests to validate that the new code works as expected.
  • [ ] If applicable, add a new test in the tests directory.
  • [ ] Update usage.md, output.md, and citation.md as appropriate.
  • [ ] Lint the code with nf-core/tools.
  • [ ] Update any diagrams or pipeline images as necessary.
  • [ ] Update MultiQC config assets/multiqc_config.yml so relevant suffixes, file name cleanup, and module plots are in the appropriate order.
  • [ ] If applicable, create a MultiQC module.
  • [ ] Add a description of the output files and, if relevant, images from the MultiQC report to docs/output.md.

To update the minimum required Nextflow version, see the Nextflow version bumping section below. For more information about pipeline contributions, see pipeline-specific contribution guidelines.

docs.title: Channel naming schemes
docs.text:
Use the following naming schemes for channels to make the channel flow easier to understand:

  • Initial process channel: ch_output_from_<process>
  • Intermediate and terminal channels: ch_<previousprocess>_for_<nextprocess>

docs.title: Default parameter values
docs.text:
Parameters should be initialised and defined with default values within the params scope in nextflow.config. They should also be documented in the pipeline JSON schema.

To update nextflow_schema.json, run:

nf-core pipelines schema build

The schema builder interface that loads in your browser should automatically update the defaults in the parameter documentation.

docs.title: Default processes resource requirements
docs.text:
If you write a local module, specify a default set of resource requirements for the process.

Sensible defaults for process resource requirements (CPUs, memory, time) should be defined in conf/base.config. Specify these with generic withLabel: selectors, so they can be shared across multiple processes and steps of the pipeline.

nf-core provides a set of standard labels that you should follow where possible, as seen in the nf-core pipeline template. These labels define resource defaults for single-core processes, modules that require a GPU, and different levels of multi-core configurations with increasing memory requirements.

Values assigned within these labels can be dynamically passed to a tool using the ${task.cpus} and ${task.memory} Nextflow variables in the script: block of a module (see an example in the modules repository).

docs.title: Nextflow version bumping
docs.text:
If you use a new feature from core Nextflow, bump the minimum required Nextflow version in the pipeline with:

nf-core pipelines bump-version --nextflow . <min_nf_version>

docs.title: Images and figures guidelines
docs.text: If you update images or graphics, follow the nf-core style guidelines.

docs.title: Pipeline specific contribution guidelines
docs.text:
• [ ] Before writing a local module, check whether nf-core/modules already has one, and install it with nf-core modules install.
  • [ ] Keep the [ meta, data ] tuple shape across module and subworkflow boundaries, so sample metadata reaches every downstream step.
  • [ ] Put local subworkflows in subworkflows/local/<name>/main.nf.
  • [ ] Add a CHANGELOG.md entry with the PR number for every user-facing change.
  • [ ] Tag fast (stub) tests with small: pull-request CI runs only tests with that tag. The extended pipeline tests (all tests tagged extended; currently chm13, clair_only, consensus, deep_only and union) run only on release or manual dispatch, so regenerate their snapshots whenever an output changes.

docs.title: IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic: Changelog
docs.text: The format is based on Keep a Changelog and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• #270 - HMF driver annotation in the report (GRCh38; CHM13 via liftover): --report_hmf_resource_dir (an oncoanalyser resource bundle, v2.x or v3.x) or the individual --report_hmf_driver_panel, --report_hmf_ensembl_data_dir, --report_hmf_known_fusions, --report_hmf_hotspots and --report_hmf_actionable_bed stage Hartwig's driver panel, Ensembl cache, known fusions, hotspots and actionable coding panel into LRSOMATICREPORT, which passes them as the report's --hmf-* flags (built in the module, so ext.args does not drop them). Report 2.3.0 then reports driver small variants per the panel's flags, amplifications/deletions from ASCAT and Wakhan separately plus Severus/SAVANA deletions (each source switchable in the browser), and known fusions with exon ranges and frame, and adds the panel as the hmf_driver gene list. On by default for GRCh38 and CHM13 (--skip_report_hmf turns it off): the new HMF_BUNDLE (bin/fetch_hmf_bundle.py) downloads and MD5-checks the genome's hosted bundle, about 5 MB, the subset of oncoanalyser v2.2.0 the report reads (IntGenomicsLab/test-datasets references/hmf/v2.2.0/, conf/igenomes.config hmf_bundle_url/hmf_bundle_md5; CHM13 pre-lifted), and publishes it under cache/hmf/ for reuse offline; the test profiles skip it. Your own resources take over from it. On --genome CHM13 a GRCh38 bundle of your own is lifted over once per run by the new HMF_LIFTOVER (bin/hmf_liftover.py, --report_hmf_liftover_chain, default the T2T consortium's public-domain grch38-chm13v2.chain, downloaded at launch; a local copy offline): whole canonical transcripts only (every exon, one contig and strand, rank order and span kept), hotspot REF re-checked on CHM13, IG/enhancer ranges and the actionable panel lifted; the lifted copy declares REFERENCE t2t, is published under pipeline_info/hmf_liftover/ and can be reused as --report_hmf_resource_dir. On any other genome the pipeline warns and skips it; a missing driver panel or Ensembl cache, or CHM13-lifted resources on GRCh38, is a launch error. hmfReportFiles() / hmfAnnotationOk() gate the workflow and the validation alike (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #269 - Added --skip_alignment (off by default) to use input BAMs/CRAMs that are already aligned to --fasta instead of realigning them with minimap2. The new PREPARE_ALIGNED module checks that every @SQ contig is in the reference with the same length and that the file is coordinate-sorted, then makes one samtools pass that sets the pipeline's read group, drops old phasing tags (and PacBio kinetics unless --keep_kinetic_data), writes --aligned_format and indexes it. Rows that fibertools-rs reads (Fiber-seq, or PacBio kinetics with m6A prediction) and unaligned rows stop the run with an error that names the row. Realigning stays the recommended path. Includes a module test, -stub pipeline tests and an extended CHM13 run (@ljwharbers).
  • #268 - The documentation site (https://intgenomicslab.github.io/lrsomatic/) is now versioned with mike and built by the Docs workflow: /latest/ follows the newest GitHub release, every release keeps its own /<version>/, and /dev/ tracks the dev branch. The MkDocs sources (mkdocs.yml, schema_render.py, docs/) are now in the repository.
  • #258 - LRSOMATICREPORT passes the run mode to the report, --run-mode paired when meta.paired_data is set and --run-mode tumour_only otherwise, instead of the report inferring it from whether normal-side QC files were staged (campaign E-F2: a pair run without mosdepth, cramino and samtools stats was badged tumour-only and given the tumour-only caveat). Requires lrsomatic_report >= 2.1.0, which this release pins. The stub writes the flag into its HTML, and the stub pipeline test checks it per sample (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - LRSOMATICREPORT is now also given variants/clairsto/<sample>.verdict_status.tsv (tumour-only) and ReConPlot's --reconplot_regions figures, reconplot/<pair>/focus/*.png, which were published but never staged (RECONPLOT_FIGURES gains a focus emit). Report 2.1.0 renders them as the tumour-only Verdict warning and the "Your regions" block that opens the ReConPlot section. The stub pipeline test now runs with --reconplot_regions and checks both relpaths, and a real-render module test stages both files and checks that the report shows both (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - Tumour-only samples get variants/clairsto/<sample>.verdict_status.tsv, saying whether ClairS-TO's Verdict tagged the calls (applied), ran and tagged nothing (skipped: purity above 0.6, or no purity/ploidy solution) or did not run (not_run), with the purity, ploidy and purity source it used (ascat from CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG, clairsto_internal with --skip_ascat) and Verdict's own reason. Until now a skip was only visible in the task's .command.out, although it leaves somatic.vcf.gz mostly germline on a high-purity tumour (73-93 % of PASS SNVs at VAF >= 0.35 on three 30x samples with ASCAT purity 0.66-0.82). The pipeline log now warns for every skipped or not_run sample, naming it with its purity and source. CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG takes the status from whether Verdict wrote tagged VCFs (it writes them only when it tags); CLAIRSTO from Verdict's tagging logs, which exist only when Verdict ran and carry its skip message. New bin/verdict_status.py, verdictStatusWarning() and tests for both paths (@ljwharbers).
  • #243 - LRSOMATICREPORT stages every other output the report reads through one generic input, two parallel lists extra_relpaths/extra_files: each file is linked at its published path under the tool's sample directory (<outdir>/<sample>/ layout), so a new report input needs no new module slot. The report now also receives SigProfiler activities, fit statistics and matrices, ShatterSeek summaries, the ecDNA outputs (AmpliconClassifier profiles, gene list and result table, the CoRAL seeds, amplicon summary and graph/cycles PNGs), SAVANA's somatic SV VCF (PoN-filtered for PacBio tumour-only), fitted purity/ploidy and VEP annotation, Padfoot's per-pair tables, ReConPlot's PNG figures, Wakhan's top-ranked integer_profile.bed and gene copy-number states, and ASCAT's metrics.txt. Each file stages in its own numbered directory, so per-pair files sharing a base name (Padfoot's by_gene.tsv, ReConPlot's figures) do not collide (@ljwharbers).
  • #243 - LRSOMATICREPORT publishes <sample>_small_variants.tsv.gz beside the HTML: the full small-variant table, written when the somatic VEP file holds at least one variant. The report tool's new --embed slim|full (which rows the HTML table embeds; default slim) has no pipeline parameter and is passed through ext.args (@ljwharbers).
  • #243 - New emits for the report: SIGPROFILER_ASSIGNMENT.out.solution_stats (Assignment_Solution/Solution_Stats/*_Samples_Stats.txt), ECDNA.out.{gene_list,result_table,seeds,summary}, PADFOOT_ANNOTATION.out.{annotated_svs,by_gene} and RECONPLOT_FIGURES.out.{genome_wide,per_chromosome}, with assertions in their stub tests, and LRSOMATICREPORT stub tests that same-named files land at their own paths and that mismatched lists fail (@ljwharbers).
  • #222 - Added ShatterSeek chromothripsis calling for every CN/SV caller pair with output for a sample (ASCAT + Severus, Wakhan + Severus, SAVANA), published to <sample>/shatterseek/<pair>/ with a per-chromosome summary, the exact ShatterSeek inputs and a figure per called chromosome; each cluster is labelled with the PCAWG high-confidence tiers (HC1, HC2, HC3; Cortes-Ciriano et al. 2020, ShatterSeek issue #22), with BH q-values at 0.2 and cut-offs overridable through ext.args. The pipeline runs upstream parklab/ShatterSeek with a build-time patch adding T2T-CHM13, inside docker.io/robertaforsyth/shatterseek (SIF twin oras://docker.io/robertaforsyth/shatterseek-sif, recipe in containers/shatterseek/); the callers are read by the ReConPlot wrapper's parsers. --skip_shatterseek, --shatterseek_genome and --shatterseek_min_svlen (intra-chromosomal SVs shorter than 150 bp are left out by default) control it (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #221 - SigProfilerAssignment now also exports the probability of each COSMIC signature for every somatic mutation (Assignment_Solution/Activities/Decomposed_Mutation_Probabilities/), e.g. to attribute a driver mutation to a signature (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #221 - Added non-stub SIGPROFILER_ASSIGNMENT nf-tests (tag small) that fit synthetic SBS96, DBS78 and ID83 matrices on GRCh38 and CHM13-T2T and check the per-mutation probabilities of every context (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #204 - Added haplotype differential methylation region (DMR) calling: with --modkit_phased set, modkit dmr pair compares methylation between the _hp1/_hp2 bedMethyl pileups over CpG islands covered in both haplotypes, and each DMR call is annotated with its nearest gene via bedtools closest. Runs automatically whenever --modkit_phased is set; turn it off with --skip_dmr. --dmr_cpg_islands_bed/--dmr_gencode_gene_bed have built-in defaults for --genome GRCh38/CHM13 and must be supplied explicitly for any other genome, or DMR is skipped with a warning rather than failing the run. Tumour/normal (cross-sample) DMR is explicitly out of scope for this PR (@YannVRB).
  • #204 - Added a real, public subworkflow-level nf-test for the DMR subworkflow (tag small), chaining MODKIT_PILEUP on the public phased, methylation-tagged test.sorted.phased.bam fixture through the full DMR chain against a small synthetic CpG-island/gene region (@YannVRB).
  • #205 - Added ecDNA and focal amplification analysis: CoRAL reconstructs amplicon structures from each tumour BAM, seeded by ASCAT's copy-number calls, and AmpliconClassifier labels each amplicon as ecDNA, BFB or linear. Runs by default on tumour samples with ASCAT calls; turn it off with --skip_coral, or keep reconstruction without classification with --skip_ampliconclassifier. CoRAL's optimisation defaults to the open-source SCIP solver rather than Gurobi: across the 1102 solver logs from the previous standalone cohort the largest model was 620 rows by 438 columns and the slowest solve took 0.49 s, so a licensed solver buys nothing at this scale, though --coral_solver gurobi_direct with --gurobi_license remains available. AmpliconClassifier's AmpliconArchitect data repository is downloaded automatically for GRCh38, checked against a pinned --aa_data_repo_md5, and can be supplied with --aa_data_repo (the reference directory or its parent); CHM13 has no published repository, so without --aa_data_repo the classifier is skipped with a warning (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - Added ascat_to_coral_bed.py and the ASCAT_TO_CORAL_BED module, converting ASCAT's cnvs.txt into the headerless BED CoRAL seeds from. Contigs are respelled to match the reference, since ASCAT writes 1 where the BAM may say chr1 and CoRAL builds its chromosome sizes from the BAM header; zero-length and inverted segments are dropped, which CoRAL's own parser would otherwise reject (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - Added stub nf-tests for the ECDNA subworkflow and ASCAT_TO_CORAL_BED (tag small), covering the seeded path, the empty-seed branch, the opt-in cycle re-extraction with plotting, the --skip_ampliconclassifier path and a run with no data repository, plus a stub test for AADATAREPO_DOWNLOAD (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #207 - The samplesheet now accepts CRAM as well as BAM (.cram in bam_tumor/bam_normal), unaligned or aligned to any assembly. An aligned CRAM is decoded with --fasta only when no contig name has a different M5 checksum in the two (checked in METAEXTRACT for CRAMINO_PRE, and inside MINIMAP2_ALIGN), otherwise from its embedded reference, UR: path or REF_PATH: given a mismatched reference, htslib decodes an embedded-reference CRAM to wrong bases (63 of 1469 test reads) and exits 0. A run resumed from an earlier version re-runs METAEXTRACT, CRAMINO_PRE, CRAMINO_POST and MINIMAP2_ALIGN for BAM input too: Nextflow hashes the script source, and this PR edits all four (CRAMINO gained a --reference argument and a FASTA input) (@ljwharbers).
  • #207 - Aligned CRAM is accepted for samples that fibertools-rs reads (a fiber = y row, or PacBio reads with kinetics while m6A prediction runs). fibertools-rs takes no reference, so aligned input of these samples, BAM or CRAM, first goes through SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP (nf-core samtools/view, samtools 1.25), which keeps the primary records as BAM and decodes a CRAM with --fasta when its M5s match, otherwise from its embedded reference, UR: path or REF_PATH; a CRAM with none of those fails there with htslib's error. On Revio and ONT fiber-seq reads aligned to GRCh38, an embedded-reference CRAM 3.0 or 3.1 gave the same predict-m6a, add-nucleosomes, fire and qc output as the BAM. METAEXTRACT emits aligned_input ('true' for a BAM or CRAM with @SQ lines) for the decision. The step runs inside the FIBERSEQ subworkflow, where the rest of the samples reach fibertools-rs as given (@ljwharbers).
  • #207 - Added tests for CRAM input (tag small): module tests of METAEXTRACT and MINIMAP2_ALIGN on CRAMs built from a test BAM (aligned with and without the reference embedded, and unaligned), against a matching and a mismatched FASTA, which check the M5 decisions and that every CRAM realigns to the same records as the BAM; a module test of SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP's filter on that BAM with secondary alignments added, as BAM and as both CRAMs; -stub pipeline tests with BAM and CRAM rows mixed in one samplesheet and with fiber-seq rows given as aligned CRAM, aligned BAM and unaligned CRAM; and a function test of the fibertools-rs input selection (@ljwharbers).
  • #207 - Added a -stub pipeline test of --aligned_format cram and bam on the extended samplesheet (tag small), which checks the replicate merge and the published bamfiles/, and a read-group check in the default test. The pipeline could not run with -stub before: the METAEXTRACT stub reported no basecalling model, and the patched LONGPHASE_PHASE stub indexed VCFs it never wrote (@ljwharbers).
  • #215 - Added optional whitelist SV calling: SEVERUS now runs a patched Severus 1.7 image (oras://docker.io/amberverhasselt/severus-sif:1.7-whitelist-6813dee), whose output without a whitelist is identical to stock 1.7, and takes an optional whitelist BED: --severus_whitelist <bed> reports every SV inside the whitelisted regions, past the read-quality, minimum-support and VNTR filters, with corroboration required for single-read junctions. Extra flags go through --severus_whitelist_args. --severus_whitelist is not supported under Conda (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #197 - Added CHM13 support for ClairS-TO's Verdict module, which tags tumour-only calls as germline, somatic or subclonal somatic; its resources were GRCh38-only, so on CHM13 germline variants leaked into somatic.vcf.gz. With --genome CHM13 --skip_ascat the pipeline builds a CHM13 resource set from the ASCAT files it already downloads and passes it as --cna_resource_dir; a prepared directory can be given with --clairsto_cna_resources (validated at launch). Without --skip_ascat tagging comes from ASCAT's own tables instead (next entry) (@ljwharbers).
  • #197 - Added CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG: when ASCAT is in the run, Verdict's germline tagging is computed from ASCAT's purity, ploidy and segments instead of Verdict's own estimate, so CLAIRSTO runs with --disable_verdict and ASCAT runs before small variant calling. Output names are unchanged. The tables the tags were computed from are published as <sample>_Tumor_Purity_Ploidy.txt and <sample>_Tumor_CNA.txt, also on --skip_ascat runs (@ljwharbers).
  • #197 - Added a stub nf-test for TUMORONLY_SMALLVAR covering both germline tagging paths (tag small) (@ljwharbers).
  • #190 - Added mutational signature analysis: SigProfilerMatrixGenerator matrices (SBS/DBS/ID) and per-sample COSMIC signature fitting with SigProfilerAssignment on the phased somatic VCF, with CHM13-T2T support via a purpose-built image (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/sigprofiler) and CHM13-renormalised COSMIC signatures; new --sigprofiler_* / --download_sigprofiler_genome / --skip_signatures parameters (@ljwharbers).
  • #188 - Added modkit_args (default --cpg --modified-bases 5mC) to control the arguments passed to modkit pileup, and modkit_phased to run the pileup with --phased on the Longphase-haplotagged BAMs, producing _hp1, _hp2 and _combined bedMethyl files per sample (@ljwharbers).
  • #176 - Added LRSOMATICREPORT as the final pipeline step: a self-contained per-sample HTML report covering small variants, structural variants, copy number and QC. Skip it with --skip_report; choose the gene panel selected on load with --report_gene_panel (@ljwharbers).
  • #176 - Added the lrsomatic_report tool to the pipeline, first vendored as source at assets/lrsomatic_report, now shipped as a container (see the entry below) (@ljwharbers).
  • #176 - Added a solution_dirs output to the WAKHAN module so its per-solution copy-number plots can be staged downstream (@ljwharbers).
  • #193 - Added VEP plugins: AlphaMissense, SIFT/PolyPhen, ClinVar and REVEL on GRCh38, and AlphaMissense plus SIFT/PolyPhen on CHM13 via protein-space lookup. Enabled by default with --genome GRCh38 or --genome CHM13 (a first GRCh38 run downloads around 1.4 GB); any --vep_* path overrides its default and --skip_vep_plugins turns the set off. CADD and EVE are opt-in behind --vep_cadd_snv/--vep_cadd_indel and --vep_eve because of their size (81 GB and 9.6 GB); prepared REVEL and EVE files are published to <outdir>/vep_plugins/ for reuse. Two lab-hosted AlphaMissense files are CC BY 4.0 with attribution in CITATIONS.md (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #189 - Added SAVANA structural variant and copy-number calling, running alongside Severus/ASCAT (@yannvrb).
  • #202 - Added Padfoot annotation of somatic SVs and CNAs for every caller pair with output for a sample, Severus + Wakhan and SAVANA, paired and tumour-only, published to <sample>/padfoot/<pair>/. Padfoot (a pinned commit of Tim-Yu/Padfoot, which adds SAVANA input) ships inside docker.io/timmy9527/padfoot-repeatmasker (oras://docker.io/timmy9527/padfoot-repeatmasker-sif under Singularity/Apptainer) with RepeatMasker on by default, so nothing is downloaded at run time and the module needs a container engine; gene copy number is labelled against the caller's fitted ploidy; --skip_padfoot and the --padfoot_* parameters control it (@Tim-Yu).
  • #202 - Added ReConPlot rearrangement and copy-number figures per CN/SV caller pair, reconplot/{severus_ascat,severus_wakhan,savana}/, with per-chromosome, genome-wide and optional focus panels plus the harmonised CN/SV tables. The wrapper ships in assets/reconplot/ and the ReConPlot R package inside docker.io/timmy9527/reconplot (oras://docker.io/timmy9527/reconplot-sif under Singularity/Apptainer; the image patches the package's genome-wide chromosome clipping), so nothing is downloaded at run time and the module needs a container engine; --skip_reconplot and the --reconplot_* parameters control it (@Tim-Yu).
  • #202 - PAIRED_SAVANA and TUMORONLY_SAVANA also emit the fitted purity/ploidy and the het-SNP allele counts, so Padfoot and ReConPlot can consume SAVANA output; ReConPlot reads SAVANA's SVs from the classified somatic VCF, since SAVANA writes no somatic BEDPE for PacBio (--pb) (@Tim-Yu).
  • #202 - Added stub nf-tests for PADFOOT_ANNOTATION and RECONPLOT_FIGURES that check every caller pair is formed (including ASCAT + Severus for tumour-only samples), unfitted samples are dropped and each task receives the top-ranked Wakhan solution's files (tag small) (@Tim-Yu).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• #270 - LRSOMATICREPORT runs lrsomatic_report 2.3.0 (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report:2.3.0 / oras://ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report-sif:2.3.0). Changes since 2.2.0: the optional HMF driver annotation section (--hmf-*); Wakhan 0.4.x output (solution_N/bed_output/*_copynumbers_segments_HP_{1,2}.bed) is read, where the copy-number section used to fall back to ASCAT; the SV table carries each breakend's orientation; HMF resources declaring their build (a CHM13 lift) are accepted on t2t reports, and where VEP's transcript ids are another namespace (CHM13's rapid-release cache) VEP's canonical transcript stands in for HMF's (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #261 - LRSOMATICREPORT runs lrsomatic_report 2.2.0 (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report:2.2.0 / oras://ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report-sif:2.2.0). Changes since 2.1.0: the ecDNA "N more CoRAL plots not embedded" note names the folder relative to the sample directory instead of an absolute work-directory path; the overview shows a warning box when the purity estimates of ASCAT, Wakhan and SAVANA differ by 0.2 or more; the full small-variant table (<sample-id>_small_variants.tsv.gz) is now also embedded in the HTML, with Download and Show all controls, unless it is larger than 5 MB gzipped, so each report grows by about 4/3 of that file's size (@ljwharbers).
  • #260 - A fiber-seq file whose reads carry no m6A calls now skips the fibertools-rs nucleosome, FIRE and QC steps (and SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP) whenever the run predicts no m6A for it, not only under --skip_m6a: ONT reads basecalled without a 6mA model, and PacBio reads without kinetics. PacBio reads with kinetics still get m6A predicted and then the fiber steps unless --skip_m6a is set, and a file whose m6a_calls is 'unknown' keeps them. The rule shares one helper with the FIBERTOOLSRS_PREDICTM6A branch (m6aPredicted), and the warning names the reason for each skipped file. The fiber-seq -stub tests give their fixtures m6A calls so they still reach the fiber steps (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - --genome GRCh38 now aligns to the NCBI no-ALT analysis set (GCA_000001405.15_GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set, staged from its byte-identical iGenomes copy Homo_sapiens/NCBI/GRCh38/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/genome.fa) instead of the GATK Homo_sapiens_assembly38.fasta, whose 261 ALT, 525 HLA and 2,385 decoy contigs minimap2 does not handle as alternates. On a 30x real-data run with a no-ALT build that kept the hs38d1 decoys, removing the ALT contigs raised Clair3's germline calls in the ALT-contig footprint from 49,085 to 167,927 (MHC 4,280 to 28,899), with calls elsewhere within 0.1 %; the new default has no decoy contigs, so reads from decoy sequence now map to the primary assembly. The 195 contigs of the new FASTA are a subset of the GATK FASTA with identical names, lengths and MD5s, so the other GRCh38 resources are unchanged. Results differ from earlier versions in ALT regions, and -resume from an earlier version realigns every sample; pass the old path with --fasta to keep it (see docs/usage.md, GRCh38 reference) (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - With --skip_m6a, a fiber-seq file whose reads carry no m6A calls now skips the fibertools-rs nucleosome, FIRE and QC steps (and SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP) with a warning naming the sample, and goes on to alignment as given, like a fiber = n row. METAEXTRACT emits the new m6a_calls ('true' when an MM tag of the first 1000 records has an A+a, T-a or ChEBI 28871 entry, 'false' when none has, 'unknown' when the records could not be read; only aux fields are decoded, so a CRAM needs no reference); 'unknown' keeps the fiber steps. On a 2 M-read PacBio fiber-seq slice without m6A these steps had reported zero m6A, nucleosomes and MSPs on every read and written a 98 GB FIRE copy of the 94 GB input. FIBERTOOLSRS_FIRE also replaces its per-read FIRE: no msp annotations on record; skipping warning (2 M lines, 214 MB of task logs on that slice) with one count line; all other output of ft fire is kept. A run resumed from an earlier version re-runs METAEXTRACT and FIBERTOOLSRS_FIRE (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - LRSOMATICREPORT runs lrsomatic_report 2.1.0 (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report:2.1.0 / oras://ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report-sif:2.1.0). Changes:
  • Severus whitelist-rescued SVs get their own hidden-by-default "rescued" tier, with a show/hide toggle in key findings, the SV table and the circos labels.
  • Failed (FAIL_*) SV records no longer count.
  • ClinVar is credited only to the gene that carries the coding or splice consequence.
  • Breakpoint and focal-deletion gene claims are checked by position.
  • Coding TMB counts unique variants and leads with SNVs.
  • ShatterSeek calls name their HC tiers, and there is a tier selector.
  • ReConPlot has a reason selector and caps the embedded per-chromosome figures at 12.
  • The phasing percentage is now of heterozygous variants.
  • Copy number 1 at high ploidy is called a "deep deletion".
  • The circos copy-number ring uses the overview's copy-number source.
  • Symbol-only gene lists get gene spans.
  • DeepSomatic genotypes are explained.
  • No absolute work-dir paths appear in the report.
  • The ASCAT tab says when ASCAT was skipped.
  • New optional inputs (--run-mode, Verdict status, ReConPlot focus figures) are wired below (@ljwharbers).
  • #243 - LRSOMATICREPORT now runs lrsomatic_report 2.0.0 (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report:2.0.0 / oras://ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report-sif:2.0.0), which adds clinical-overview, genomic-instability (ShatterSeek, ecDNA), signature and ReConPlot sections and reads SAVANA and Padfoot. Wakhan's interactive HTML plots and heatmap are no longer staged or embedded; the report draws the top-ranked solution from integer_profile.bed, and the HTML plots stay in wakhan/. Each sample's report now waits for the run's last output of those tools, since several are optional per sample or ignored on failure, so there is no per-sample count to group on; this gives up the per-sample rendering of #200 for the report step (@ljwharbers).
  • #242 - Right-sized default resource requests from execution traces of ~30x ONT and PacBio runs (pairs and tumour-only, GRCh38 and CHM13), in a new withName section of conf/base.config. Lowered where requests were an order of magnitude above use: FIBERTOOLSRS_NUCLEOSOMES/FIRE/QC (200/144 GB -> 8 GB, 8-16 cpus; peaks <= 3.1 GB), FIBERTOOLSRS_PREDICTM6A (200 GB / 16 h -> 16 GB / 24 h at 24 cpus, for ~185 cpu-hours and a 7 GB peak), GERMLINE_VEP (16 cpus / 16 GB), SOMATIC_VEP/SV_VEP/VEP_SAVANA (24 / 144 GB -> 6 / 24 GB), the per-sample bcftools steps of the consensus, Verdict and phasing chains (6 / 36 GB -> 2 / 4 GB), LONGPHASE_MODCALL_* (12 -> 2 cpus, as it runs single-threaded; 64 GB), LRSOMATICREPORT (1 cpu / 32 GB), MOSDEPTH (4 / 8 GB), DeepVariant/DeepSomatic call_variants on CPU (144 -> 48 GB), and the labels of SIGPROFILER_MATRIXGENERATOR (process_single), CORAL_PLOT and AMPLICONCLASSIFIER (process_low). Raised where 30x data reaches the default: WAKHAN 36 -> 72 GB (38-64 GB on tumour-only samples), SEVERUS 36 -> 64 GB (32 GB on ONT pairs), SAVANA_RUN/SAVANA_TO 72 -> 96 GB, CRAMINO 2 -> 4 cpus. All keep attempt scaling. The fibertools tasks that request a GPU under --use_gpu keep their previous requests (24 cpus / 144 GB / 16 h), as that path was not measured. docs/usage.md now lists the measured needs of the heaviest steps at ~30x (@ljwharbers).
  • #250 - Resource defaults resized from 30x real-data runs: SAVANA_RUN 96 to 128 GB (paired peaks up to 118 GB), DEEPSOMATIC_MAKEEXAMPLES 144 to 192 GB (peak 120 GB), LRSOMATICREPORT 32 to 16 GB (peak 9 GB); BCFTOOLS_CALLER_CONSENSUS joins the small bcftools block (2 cpus / 4 GB, was 6 / 36 GB for under 1 GB), and the removed BCFTOOLS_ISEC, NORM_REJOIN, SORT_CONSENSUS and DS_VERDICT_*/DS_GERMLINE_REJOIN names leave its selector (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - CLAIRS, DEEPSOMATIC_MAKEEXAMPLES, DEEPSOMATIC_CALLVARIANTS (CPU) and FIBERTOOLSRS_PREDICTM6A (CPU) request 48 cpus instead of 24; memory and time are unchanged. At 24 cpus paired DeepSomatic took 15.9 h of a 17.75 h 30x ONT pair run (make_examples 6.4 h, call_variants 8.5 h; 3.7 h and 5.4 h at 48), PacBio ClairS 6.2-6.4 h (3.6 h at 48) and m6A prediction 5.7-6.3 h at 97 % cpu efficiency (3.8 h at 64). DEEPSOMATIC_CALLVARIANTS under --use_gpu keeps 8 cpus (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - docs/usage.md notes that float read tags (Dorado's qs, du, sd) keep only the 6 significant digits samtools fastq -T writes on their way through minimap2 -y (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - docs/usage.md lists the small differences to expect between runs on identical input (ClairS/DeepSomatic ±1-2 PASS records between thread counts, SAVANA copy-number segmentation and purity ±0.01, SAVANA and Severus ±1-2 SVs) (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - docs/usage.md describes every option of the whitelist Severus build (--whitelist-single-read reciprocal|any|off, --whitelist-reciprocal-dist, --whitelist-allow-intra-region, --whitelist-enforce-mapq, passed through --severus_whitelist_args) and the INFO/INSIDE_WHITELIST/WL_RESCUE tags, with a warning that --whitelist-single-read any floods 30x WGS (9,388 of 9,711 somatic SVs rescued on a 30x ONT pair, 314 without a whitelist) and that rescued SVs reach ShatterSeek and ReConPlot (@ljwharbers).
  • #245 - SHATTERSEEK runs upstream parklab/ShatterSeek (+CHM13 patch, robertaforsyth/shatterseek:1.1-3b3f4cd-chm13, SIF twin oras://docker.io/robertaforsyth/shatterseek-sif) instead of the robert-a-forsyth fork, at the author's request (@ljwharbers).
  • #240 - A samplesheet whose replicate rows the per-type merge would mis-handle now stops the run at launch, naming the sample: rows of one sample that mix "has normal" and "no normal" (the tumour rows were never merged and the run aborted after alignment with a bare Join mismatch), a normal file repeated across rows (it was merged with itself, doubling normal depth), a file given as both tumour and normal, and duplicate tumor_replicate/normal_replicate numbers within a sample, including the all-blank case (the replicates shared output names and @RG IDs). A tumour file repeated across rows only warns. Single-row samples, tumour-only replicates and the paired T1,N1,1,1/T2,N2,2,2 form are unchanged. New stub test tests/samplesheet_replicates.nf.test (@ljwharbers).
  • #247 - Rows of one sample that differ in platform, sex or fiber now stop the run at launch, naming the sample and each row's value; docs/usage.md asked for these to match but nothing checked it. The caller-model mismatch error (raised after METAEXTRACT) labels each file by type and replicate (tumor_rep1=..., tumor_rep2=...) instead of tumor= twice, and no longer tells users who already set the model column to set it explicitly. New cases in the utils_nfcore_lrsomatic_pipeline function tests and tests/samplesheet_replicates.nf.test (@ljwharbers).
  • #235 - Raised the minimum Nextflow version from 25.10.4 to 26.04.0; users on Nextflow 25.10 must upgrade. Nextflow 25.10 compiles each workflow body into one string and fails with String too long above 65,535 characters; the LRSOMATIC workflow body is close to that limit, and Nextflow 26.04 has no such limit. The bump also follows nf-core: nf-schema goes from 2.7.3 to 3.0.0, which needs Nextflow 26.04, and the utils_nfschema_plugin subworkflow is updated to the nf-core master that targets it, so paramsSummaryMap no longer takes the workflow object and paramsHelp takes the parameter as a parameter: option. The nf-test CI matrix, fix-linting.yml, the README badge and the RO-Crate metadata now say 26.04.0. The launch-validation function tests now look for the error message on stderr as well as stdout, because Nextflow 26.10 prints console output to stderr when ANSI logging is off (nextflow-io/nextflow#7741), so 19 of them failed on the latest-everything CI shards. --show_hidden is converted to a boolean before it reaches nf-schema, because Nextflow 26 passes a bare --show_hidden as the string 'true' and nf-schema 3.0.0 failed on it with a String cannot be cast to Boolean error (fixed upstream after 3.0.0, nextflow-io/nf-schema#237) (@ljwharbers).
  • #233 - Updated to the nf-core template for nf-core/tools 4.2.2, which moves the CI's eWaterCycle/setup-apptainer action from v2 to v3 (@ljwharbers).
  • #221 - --sigprofiler_matrix_args now rejects --bed_file, --exome and --seqInfo False, as the per-mutation signature probabilities are built from every mutation's SigProfilerMatrixGenerator seqinfo (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #207 - Aligned and haplotagged reads are now CRAM 3.0 with the reference embedded instead of BAM, from MINIMAP2_ALIGN onwards; bamfiles/ holds <sample>_<type>.cram + .crai. The new --aligned_format parameter (cram by default, or bam) keeps BAM throughout for tools that cannot read CRAM. On chr20 of three real samples CRAM is 33 % (ONT), 52 % (older PacBio) and 69 % (Revio) smaller, with identical records. Version 3.0 because Clair3 and ClairS-TO's Verdict bundle an htslib that cannot decode 3.1 and then call nothing without failing; the embedded reference (1-7 % of the file) because ClairS, ClairS-TO, Severus and SAVANA open the reads without the FASTA. CRAMINO_POST and SAMTOOLS_MERGE now get the FASTA (ASCAT does not: its image has no ref.fasta argument, and it reads the embedded reference); CLAIRSTO deletes its intermediate haplotagged copy of the tumour reads; the uBAM's own RG tag is dropped before alignment, since CRAM keeps one read group per record and kept the basecaller's. That change alters MINIMAP2_ALIGN in both formats, so a run resumed from an earlier version realigns every sample, also with --aligned_format bam. LONGPHASE_MODCALL moves from longphase 2.0.1 to 2.0.2: 2.0.1 reads CRAM through the wrong iterator call and called about 28 % fewer methylation sites on CRAM than on BAM, a different number every run, which shifted the phasing and every haplotype-resolved output; 2.0.2 gives identical, deterministic results for both formats (@ljwharbers).
  • #227 - Cleared the pipeline-level nf-core lint warnings. manifest.version and the .nf-core.yml template version are now 1.2.0dev; the 13 flat subworkflows/local/*.nf files moved to subworkflows/local/<name>/main.nf; skip_modkit is in the skip options group and six parameters got schema descriptions; --autocorrelation is now a boolean (default false), as docs/usage.md already described it, so a bare --autocorrelation flag passes validation; template TODOs are resolved, including a pipeline citation in the MultiQC methods description and pipeline-specific contribution guidelines; and the stray lint_log.txt debug log is removed (@ljwharbers).
  • #224 - Updated to the nf-core template for nf-core/tools 4.2.1. Bumps nf-schema to 2.7.3 (needed for Nextflow 26.04) and nft-utils to 1.2.1, sets manifest.diagram to the existing metro map (assets/lrsomatic_1.0.png), replaces fix_linting.yml with the reusable fix-linting.yml from nf-core/actions, adds recommended VS Code extensions, and stops workflow.onComplete from blocking on the MultiQC report. The linting workflow keeps running plain pre-commit rather than the template's prek-action (@ljwharbers).
  • #224 - Dropped ext.use_gpu from the GPU resource labels, following the template. CLAIR3 now reads params.use_gpu instead of task.ext.use_gpu, the same param that picks its label and container, as DeepVariant, DeepSomatic and fibertools already do (@ljwharbers).
  • #204 - With --modkit_phased set and haplotype DMR running, 5hmC is appended to --modified-bases whenever --modkit_args names 5mC without it, so the published modkit_pileup/*_{hp1,hp2,combined}.bed.gz now carry a 5hmC row next to each 5mC row. modkit dmr pair rejects bedMethyl rows whose valid coverage includes uncounted (N_other) calls, which ONT SUP data calling both 5mC and 5hmC produces under the --cpg --modified-bases 5mC default. Runs with --skip_dmr, without --modkit_phased, or without DMR references keep --modkit_args exactly as given (@YannVRB).
  • #205 - Moved the fiber-seq steps into a FIBERSEQ subworkflow and the AmpliconArchitect MD5 default into aaDataRepoMd5(), because with dev merged the LRSOMATIC workflow body exceeded the 65,535-character limit on a compiled string and failed to compile; behaviour is unchanged (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - --download_sigprofiler_genome now defaults to true, so a run without --sigprofiler_genome_dir installs the SigProfiler genome instead of stopping at launch; a given directory still wins (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - Every small-variant path now rejoins each arm to one record per position (bcftools norm -m +any) before Longphase, which cannot take two records at one position; single-caller runs previously passed an SNV and an indel at the same base (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - In tumour-only mode with --smallvar_filter_pass, ClairS-TO germline calls that fail another filter (e.g. LowQual;NonSomatic) are dropped unless Verdict tags them germline; DeepVariant germline calls are PASS-filtered whenever DeepSomatic is not selected, so RefCall records never enter the germline arm (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - INFO/DS_VERDICT is now Number=. and carries a multi-valued DeepSomatic FILTER comma-separated instead of a raw ; that split the INFO field (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - ASCAT_TO_CORAL_BED now writes 0-based BED (ASCAT is 1-based), keeps single-SNP segments and tiles each contig without gaps, so CoRAL no longer silently drops breakpoints that fell between ASCAT segments. With --coral_run_cycle, reconstruction skips its own cycle decomposition; otherwise --coral_cycle_decomp_alpha is passed to it (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #200 - In tumour-only mode with both deepvariant and deepsomatic selected, DeepVariant's PASS germline calls are now kept only where DeepSomatic's verdict is GERMLINE or PON (INFO/DS_VERDICT); with deepvariant alone they are unfiltered and may include somatic variants (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #200 - The phased somatic VCF is now split from the merged germline+somatic VCF by an INFO/SOMATIC provenance flag (new VCFTAG module) instead of by position, so germline records at somatic coordinates no longer leak into it; ClairS-TO germline records keep their original FILTER in INFO/ORIG_FILTER (@robert-a-forsyth). The merge and the INFO/SOMATIC flag were removed again in #266 (see Fixed); INFO/ORIG_FILTER stays.
  • #200 - Added --smallvar_filter_pass (default true), which restricts each small variant caller's output to PASS records before the caller consensus, phasing, VEP and the report; the published per-caller VCFs are unchanged (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #201 - CLAIRSTO and CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG now pull the fork image from Docker Hub: oras://docker.io/ljwharbers/clairs-to-sif:0.5.1-verdict-chm13-c0687e8-flat under Singularity/Apptainer and docker.io/ljwharbers/clairs-to:0.5.1-verdict-chm13-c0687e8-flat otherwise, instead of ghcr.io/ljwharbers/clairs-to. The -cpu SIF on ghcr failed with PROTOCOL_ERROR on slow links: ghcr redirects every blob download to an Azure URL that expires at the next 5-minute mark and resets a stream still open then, and Apptainer resumes neither an oras:// nor a docker:// download. Docker Hub's download URLs are valid for 50 minutes and only checked when the request starts. -flat is the same software copied into an empty image in a few layers (3.3 GB instead of 7 GB); the software and its outputs are unchanged. docs/usage.md describes pullTimeout, Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit, pre-pulling, and how to recover the remaining oras://ghcr.io SIFs resumably (@ljwharbers).
  • #199 - CLAIRSTO and CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG now run the -cpu rebuild of the fork image (0.5.1-verdict-chm13-c0687e8-cpu), which swaps PyTorch's CUDA build for the CPU build of the same version. The software is otherwise unchanged, but the Apptainer SIF drops from 6.53 GB to 3.46 GB. The old image could not be pulled on a normal VSC link: Apptainer fetches an oras:// SIF as a single unresumable stream, and the signed blob URL ghcr redirects to expires on a 15-minute wall-clock boundary, so 6.53 GB needed 7.3 MB/s sustained and was otherwise cut mid-transfer with PROTOCOL_ERROR (@ljwharbers).
  • #197 - CLAIRSTO now runs ghcr.io/ljwharbers/clairs-to:0.5.1-verdict-chm13-c0687e8 (ClairS-TO 0.5.1) instead of docker.io/hkubal/clairs-to:v0.4.2: a fork that lets Verdict read its CNA resources from --cna_resource_dir, fixes four places where Verdict's Python port of ASCAT departed from R, and disables Verdict with a warning when its resources cannot be read. GRCh38 results move as well as CHM13 ones. Revert to the upstream image once HKU-BAL/ClairS-TO carries these changes. The module also selects the SIF under -profile apptainer and sets explicit output prefixes (@ljwharbers).
  • #196 - LRSOMATICREPORT now runs lrsomatic_report v1.6.0 from ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report:1.6.0 (oras://ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report-sif:1.6.0 under Singularity/Apptainer) instead of the source vendored at assets/lrsomatic_report, which is deleted; updating the tool is now a tag bump. The image is linux/amd64 only and Conda is not supported for this step: the module errors under -profile conda/mamba, conda is dropped from the nf-test CI matrix, and --skip_report gives a conda run (@ljwharbers).
  • #196 - Builtin gene panels moved from the tool into this repository at assets/gene_lists/ and reach the report through --gene-lists-dir, so adding a panel needs no report-tool release; --report_gene_panel validation reads that directory (@ljwharbers).
  • #196 - Removed --report_src; render with an unreleased tool by pinning a container tag instead (@ljwharbers).
  • #196 - The report's small-variant table now shows the VEP plugin annotations from #193 (AlphaMissense, ClinVar, CADD, REVEL, EVE, and SIFT/PolyPhen on CHM13) as separate class and score columns, present only when the annotated VCF declared the field, with an "Annotation sources" footnote. The v1.4.0 to v1.6.0 releases also fix the SV table's panel_hit column, add the optional applies_to panel column (next entry) and make the footer read the tool version at render time (@ljwharbers).
  • #196 - Rebuilt the builtin lymphoid panel from two curated NHL lists (234 rows, up from 72) and scoped its genes per table with the new optional applies_to column (snv, sv or blank for both). Four upstream rows were corrected (EWSR1, KDM6B and SIK3 hg38 coordinates; PRKBC to PRKCB; RCK to DDX6; duplicate FAM46C dropped); see assets/gene_lists/README.md. sarcoma is untouched (@ljwharbers).
  • #188 - MODKIT_PILEUP now runs modkit pileup with --cpg --modified-bases 5mC by default; the previous unfiltered pileup produced 30-45 GB per sample, so reruns report only 5mC at CpG sites. Set --modkit_args='' (the = form; --modkit_args '' reaches the pipeline as true) or an empty modkit_args entry in a params file to get the previous output (@ljwharbers).
  • #186 - Re-synced the vendored lrsomatic_report to v1.3.0, which adds tickbox dropdown filters on the categorical columns of both variant tables and turns the report's gene panel selector into checkboxes (@ljwharbers).
  • #176 - Re-synced the vendored lrsomatic_report to v1.3.2: facet dropdown counts follow the active filters, opening a facet menu no longer resets the table's horizontal scroll, a flatter clinical theme, and inline code comments trimmed to one line (@ljwharbers).
  • #186 - --report_gene_panel now takes a comma-separated list, so several panels can be applied at once: a variant or SV is kept if it hits any of them. Panel values are also validated at launch instead of failing inside the report task (@ljwharbers).
  • #184 - Replaced the CHM13 Severus panel of normals with the merged 1000 Genomes + ASAP panel (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #183 - Updated to the nf-core template for nf-core/tools 4.1.0. Adds the check-added-large-files, check-merge-conflict and block-pipeline-outdir pre-commit hooks, a process_low_memory resource label, and a split-out pr-comment.yml workflow. conf/igenomes.config was converted to the template's strict-syntax params.genomes map literal, and the MultiQC module was bumped to 1.35 (@ljwharbers).
  • #183 - Raised the minimum Nextflow version to 25.10.4, following the template, and bumped the nf-test CI matrix to match (@ljwharbers).
  • #183 - Filled in the manifest.contributors contribution fields: @ljwharbers and @robert-a-forsyth as author and maintainer, all other contributors as author. Previously empty, which left the RO-Crate metadata without any authors (@ljwharbers).
  • #183 - Added @AmberVerhasselt to manifest.contributors as a contributor and to the README credits, and expanded @ljwharbers' affiliation to match the other core contributors. RO-Crate metadata updated to match (@ljwharbers).
  • #183 - Set @laulambr's affiliation to the same three-part VIB/KU Leuven string as the other core contributors (@ljwharbers).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• #266 - The phase of variants/phased/somatic_smallvariants.vcf.gz now agrees with the germline VCF and the haplotagged BAMs (#265). It came from a second LongPhase run on the tumour (LONGPHASE_PHASE_SOMATIC) with its own blocks and an arbitrary haplotype 1 per block, so a somatic SNV marked 1|0 was on the HP:2 reads about as often as on HP:1 (somatic VCF haplotype = alt-read HP for 60 % of SNVs on two paired 30x runs, 74-77 % tumour-only; PS matched 35-70 %). The new PHASE_SOMATIC_FROM_READS (pysam, bin/phase_somatic_from_reads.py) phases each heterozygous somatic SNV/indel from the HP/PS of its alt reads in the haplotagged tumour BAM (at least 3 tagged alt reads, at least 80 % on one haplotype) and adds FORMAT/AHP with the alt reads on HP1, HP2 and untagged. Tumour-only samples also need at least 3 tagged reads on the other haplotype at the site (FORMAT/OHP), because their haplotags, built from a germline phase on tumour reads, can put both haplotypes' reads on one HP; records failing it stay in the VCF, unphased. This replaces LONGPHASE_PHASE_SOMATIC, LONGPHASE_MODCALL_SOMATIC and the steps that fed it (REJOIN_SOMATIC, TAG_SOMATIC/TAG_GERMLINE, SOMATIC_ALT/SOMATIC_NONALT, GERMLINE_ANCHORS, the somatic concat/sort/view), so the somatic VCF keeps the callers' records (more than one per position is possible) and neither phased VCF carries INFO/SOMATIC/INFO/GERMLINE any more. A run resumed from an earlier version re-runs germline phasing, haplotagging and everything downstream (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - ENSEMBLVEP_DOWNLOAD reports its perl-math-cdf version again (it was empty in lrsomatic_software_mqc_versions.yml): the nf-core module's version command escaped $Math::CDF::VERSION once, so the shell expanded it to nothing. Patched the way upstream nf-core/modules fixed it. The version command is part of the task hash, so a resumed --download_vep_cache run downloads the cache once more (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - Published indexes are no longer older than their data file (htslib's The index file is older than the data file warning on the published gVCFs). Nextflow copies a task's files in parallel and gives each copy the time it finished, so a large VCF could land after its index; workflow.output.copyAttributes = true now keeps the work-directory timestamps, where the index is always the newer file (@ljwharbers).
  • #258 - MULTIQC no longer re-runs on every -resume: its inputs are sorted by file name instead of arriving in completion order, the workflow summary leaves out the per-launch runName and trace_report_suffix (and shows the session id, which -resume keeps), and the methods description quotes the command line without -resume and no longer expands the whole ${workflow} object in a YAML comment of assets/methods_description_template.yml (@ljwharbers).
  • #249 - A Padfoot, ReConPlot, ShatterSeek, CoRAL (reconstruct, cycle, plot) or AmpliconClassifier task that the scheduler loses (Slurm NODE_FAIL, CANCELLED by root; Nextflow exit status Integer.MAX_VALUE) is now retried once instead of being silently ignored while the run still exits 0. These steps share one policy in conf/modules.config: retry a kill (exit 130-145, 104, 175-177 or Integer.MAX_VALUE) up to maxRetries, ignore any other failure; CoRAL and AmpliconClassifier also gain 104 and 175-177, and their module tests now fail on an error instead of ignoring it. The default policy in conf/base.config also retries Integer.MAX_VALUE, which previously stopped the run. A workflow nf-test checks the policy for all twelve process names (@ljwharbers).
  • #248 - Unaligned input no longer gets a second copy of minimap2's own tags: MINIMAP2_ALIGN now drops tp, cm, s1, s2, nn, ms, de, dv, rl, zd, cs, cg, ds from every input before minimap2 -y, not only from aligned input. Dorado uBAMs that were once aligned can keep zd (minimap2's z-drop split flag), which minimap2 then wrote again, so about 10,000 reads per 30x ONT CRAM carried two zd tags and failed strict SAM validation. A run resumed from an earlier version re-runs MINIMAP2_ALIGN and everything after it for unaligned input (@ljwharbers).
  • #246 - Fixed --download_vep_cache failing every run: ENSEMBLVEP_DOWNLOAD's ext.args was commented out, so vep_install started its interactive full install (Ensembl API, BioPerl, htslib from git) and exited on the missing git. It now gets --AUTO c --CONVERT --NO_BIOPERL --NO_HTSLIB --NO_TEST --NO_UPDATE, as in nf-core/sarek, and installs only the cache (GRCh38 v113: 23.3 GiB in 27 min). The -stub test of the option missed this, since the module's stub ignores ext.args; it now checks the resolved ext.args (@ljwharbers).
  • #243 - docs/output.md names WhatsHap's outputs as published, qc/whatshap_stats/<sample>_whatshap_stats.{tsv,gtf,log}, instead of sample.stats.tsv and a sample.blocklist.tsv the pipeline never writes (@ljwharbers).
  • #241 - The tumour-only DeepVariant germline arm (with deepsomatic selected) no longer publishes genotypes DeepVariant never made: the DeepSomatic-verdict chain split DeepVariant's records per allele, selected and rejoined them, so e.g. C>CCG,CG 1/2 became C>CCG 1/0 and G>GTT,GTTT 2/2 became G>GTT 0/0 (28,705 1/0, 87 2/0 and 933 0/0 records on a PacBio tumour). DS_GERMLINE_SELECT (now BCFTOOLS_CALLER_CONSENSUS, replacing DS_VERDICT_SPLIT_DS/_DV, DS_VERDICT_SITES, DS_VERDICT_ANNOTATE and DS_GERMLINE_REJOIN) publishes DeepVariant's own PASS records, unchanged, whose called alleles all carry a DeepSomatic GERMLINE/PON verdict; INFO/DS_VERDICT is no longer added (@ljwharbers).
  • #241 - --smallvar_filter_pass false with DeepSomatic no longer crashes the run (REJOIN_SOMATIC: could not merge FORMAT tag NAF). The DeepVariant (paired germline) and DeepSomatic filters now always run: with the flag off they keep calls whose genotype carries an ALT allele and whose FILTER is PASS or LowQual, but never RefCall/NoCall records (40.4 M and 1.0 M on a 30x ONT pair) nor DeepSomatic's GERMLINE/PON verdicts. The new DEEPSOMATIC_FILTER step also declares DeepSomatic 1.10's FORMAT/NAF as Number=A (it is declared Number=R but written once per ALT allele) before any record join; the published DeepSomatic VCF is unchanged (@ljwharbers).
  • #241 - The all (union) combine mode no longer drops a caller's second allele at one position: BCFTOOLS_CALLER_UNION deduplicates with bcftools norm -d exact instead of -d all, so e.g. a Clair3 SNV and a 47 bp deletion starting at the same base are both kept (and joined into one record before phasing, as before); 4 Clair3 calls restored on a 30x ONT genome (@ljwharbers).
  • #241 - The consensus combine mode no longer publishes genotypes that neither caller made (e.g. DeepVariant C>A,G 2/2 and Clair3 C>A 0/1 gave C>A 0/0; 13,188 0/0 and 4,383 1/0 records on a 30x ONT germline set). The new BCFTOOLS_CALLER_CONSENSUS module (replacing BCFTOOLS_ISEC, BCFTOOLS_SORT_CONSENSUS and BCFTOOLS_NORM_REJOIN) matches the alleles each caller's genotype carries and publishes the priority caller's own records unchanged, where every called allele is shared; sites where the callers agree on only one of several called alleles are left out (@ljwharbers).
  • #244 - Padfoot now produces output on CHM13. Its microhomology step reads each 51-bp samtools faidx window as one line, and samtools keeps the FASTA's own line width, so with the 50-column iGenomes CHM13 genome.fa every PADFOOT_* task failed with ValueError: sequence has zero length, was ignored under its errorStrategy, and nothing was published under <sample>/padfoot/. When the .fai shows a contig wrapped at fewer than 51 columns, PADFOOT now hands Padfoot a 60-column copy (samtools faidx -n 60), deleted when the task ends; GRCh38 and other FASTAs wrapped at 51 columns or more are passed through unchanged. New module test on a 50-column FASTA (tag small) (@ljwharbers).
  • #240 - The per-sample report now receives the WhatsHap phasing statistics: <id>_whatshap_stats.tsv joins the report's tumour-side QC inputs, so its Phasing block and "Phased variants" card are filled instead of "WhatsHap phasing statistics not found" (@ljwharbers).
  • #240 - Documentation fixes from the real-data campaign: samplesheet sex is male/female; the nonexistent --normal_fiber is replaced by --skip_normalfiber; the multiple-runs section describes per-file alignment and per-type merging, the replicate columns and the valid paired encoding; re-used pipeline output needs the model columns; CRAM decoding via UR:; --smallvar_filter_pass false keeps the tumour-only ClairS-TO somatic split PASS-only; ClairS-TO Verdict tags nothing above a purity of 0.6, which leaves tumour-only somatic sets mostly germline; Padfoot fails on the 50-column iGenomes CHM13 FASTA; the T2T VEP cache has no known-variant or frequency data (@ljwharbers).
  • #240 - A sample lost before SEVERUS (e.g. by a step skipped or ignored under its errorStrategy) no longer aborts the whole run at report assembly with Invalid method invocation call: the report joins emitted it as a short tuple without meta, which the fixed-arity filter closure could not take. Such a sample now gets no report and a warning; the other samples are reported as before. New stub test tests/report_without_severus.nf.test (@ljwharbers).
  • #239 - PacBio kinetics (fi, fp, ri, rp, and per-subread ip/pw) are dropped from every PacBio read at alignment unless --keep_kinetic_data is set, which now keeps them everywhere. Before, they stayed on the 2-3 % of reads ft predict-m6a gave no m6A call (about 3-4 GB per 30x CRAM), and on every read of samples that skip m6A prediction (--skip_m6a, --skip_fiber, normals under --skip_normalfiber). A run resumed from an earlier version re-runs MINIMAP2_ALIGN and everything after it for PacBio samples; ONT samples are not affected by this change (@ljwharbers).
  • #239 - The published BAM/CRAM of ONT samples keeps the basecalling model as DS:basecall_model=<model> in its read group, so it can be fed back into the pipeline without filling the samplesheet model columns; before, the model was lost and the run failed at Clair3 model selection. A run resumed from an earlier version re-runs MINIMAP2_ALIGN and everything after it for ONT samples whose input names a model (@ljwharbers).
  • #239 - --download_vep_cache true no longer aborts the run with Not a valid path value type: java.util.ArrayList: the downloaded cache was passed on as [[:], [meta, cache]] in a queue channel, which could also have fed only one VEP task. It is now a value channel shaped like the local cache, so every VEP task gets it (@ljwharbers).
  • #239 - --use_gpu no longer puts FIBERTOOLSRS_NUCLEOSOMES, FIBERTOOLSRS_FIRE and FIBERTOOLSRS_PREDICTM6A on GPU labels: their image is the CPU fibertools-rs build, so they held a GPU at 0 % while running on the CPU. The use_gpu docs and schema help now name the steps that use a GPU (DeepVariant/DeepSomatic call_variants, Clair3) and say that their GPU images support GPUs up to Hopper (compute capability 9.0); on a B200 call_variants fails with CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PTX (@ljwharbers).
  • #239 - FIBERTOOLSRS_QC output of samples with several input files is named <id>_rep<N>_qc.txt, so replicates no longer overwrite each other in qc/<type>/fibertoolsrs/; single-file samples keep <id>_qc.txt (@ljwharbers).
  • #239 - Realigning aligned input (BAM or CRAM) no longer keeps the old alignment's tags: samtools reset only dropped its default list, so minimap2 -y wrote the old minimap2 tags (tp, cm, s1, s2, nn, ms, de, rl) a second time on 99.6 % of records and kept stale HP/PS/PQ phasing from a haplotagged input. Aligned input now drops these and other alignment and phasing tags (a deny-list, see docs/usage.md). Base modifications and read-level tags are kept. Unaligned input is not affected by this change: it still drops only RG, plus the PacBio kinetics described in the kinetics entry above (@ljwharbers).
  • #239 - WAKHAN now stages the FASTA index next to the FASTA. Without it, Wakhan's parallel samtools mpileup workers each built <fasta>.fai in the task dir at once, and a worker that read a half-written index failed the task and the run (@ljwharbers).
  • #237 - Fixed haplotype DMR calling (--modkit_phased) running for only one BAM per run: the reference channel the DMR subworkflow built for MODKIT_DMR with combine was a one-item queue channel, so MODKIT_DMR and DMR_NEAREST_GENE ran once, for whichever BAM arrived first, and every other BAM (the normal of a pair, other samples) silently got no DMR table. It is now a value channel, and the DMR subworkflow test runs a tumour and a normal and requires a DMR task for each (@ljwharbers).
  • #237 - Fixed SVs longer than 10 Mb being dropped from SV_VEP and VEP_SAVANA output: VEP skips anything above its default --max_sv_size (10,000,000) and only notes it in its unpublished warnings file, which on real samples lost 28 of 23,240 (CCS15-ONT) and 3 of 18,784 (BL5) Severus SVs, including 7 and 3 somatic events the report annotates. Both steps now pass --max_sv_size 250000000 ahead of --vep_args, so a value given there still wins. SVs on contigs the VEP cache does not cover are still skipped (@ljwharbers).
  • #237 - Fixed DEEPSOMATIC_POSTPROCESSVARIANTS and DEEPVARIANT_POSTPROCESSVARIANTS hanging until the walltime on deeper samples. When the step runs short of memory it does not fail: the kernel OOM-kills some of its pool workers, the pool respawns them without re-running their partitions, and the task waits at 0 % CPU with no error until it is killed, so an undersized memory request burns the whole time limit silently. On a 30x matched ONT pair with --generate_gvcf (12 cpus), paired DeepSomatic hung for 6 h at process_high's 72 GB (5 of 12 workers OOM-killed) and finished in 1 h 01 min at 192 GB (peak RSS 133.6 GB); DeepVariant on the normal peaked at 69.2 GB of 72 GB. Both now request memory per cpu, never less than 8 cpus' worth: DeepSomatic 16 GB per cpu for a pair and 8 GB per cpu tumour-only, DeepVariant 8 GB per cpu (192, 96 and 96 GB at process_high's 12 cpus, doubled on a retry with the cpus), and 4.h * task.attempt instead of process_short's fixed 1 h, which a retry could not extend. docs/usage.md says to set resourceLimits on machines with less memory (@ljwharbers).
  • #237 - Fixed the GRCh38 AmpliconArchitect data repository being downloaded without its pinned MD5 check. aaDataRepoMd5() read a params.aa_data_repo_url that was assigned in the workflow and is not visible in the utils script, so the URL looked overridden and the MD5 was dropped (with an "undefined parameter" warning on every run). The resolved URL is now passed in as an argument (@ljwharbers).
  • #237 - Declared --keep_kinetic_data (keep the PacBio kinetics tags on every read: ft predict-m6a --keep, and no removal at alignment) and --keep_all_calls (ft predict-m6a --all-calls), both default false, and --outdir_cache (where the downloaded VEP cache and SigProfiler genome are published, default <outdir>/cache). conf/modules.config already read all three, so every run warned "Access to undefined parameter". Defaults are unchanged (@ljwharbers).
  • #238 - Fixed three stub blocks that stopped -stub-run from reaching large parts of the pipeline (real runs are unaffected). The nf-core UNZIP stub (now patched locally) wrote an empty directory, so ASCAT got no reference files, never ran, and the strict joins on its output aborted every stub run with ASCAT on. The patched SEVERUS stub wrote .vcf where the outputs expect .vcf.gz, so WAKHAN, SV_VEP and every *_SEVERUS_* Padfoot/ReConPlot/ShatterSeek task were silently skipped. The patched BCFTOOLS_QUERY stub touched the .tbi before running tabix, which refuses to overwrite it, killing every stub run with two callers per arm (@ljwharbers).
  • #236 - Paired SAVANA_CNA no longer receives the genome's contigs file: savana cna has no --contigs option (only savana run and savana to do), so every matched tumour-normal run with SAVANA on failed with unrecognized arguments: --contigs, on GRCh38 and CHM13 alike. The test profiles ignored every SAVANA_CNA failure, which hid it from CI; they now ignore only the expected no-fit on the chr19 slice (exit 1) and fail on argument errors (exit 2), for SAVANA_TO too. Paired copy-number calling still covers only chr1-22, chrX and chrY: savana cna hard-codes that list (@ljwharbers).
  • #222 - The ReConPlot wrapper's SAVANA VCF parser re-expresses a _2 breakend from its mate's side before collapsing mates: SAVANA writes BP_NOTATION in (_1, _2) order on both records, so a junction whose _2 record came first in the file paired the second breakend's position with the first breakend's orientation (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #222 - RECONPLOT and SHATTERSEEK unset R_HOME before running R. Apptainer forwards the host environment, and with a host R_HOME set (as with a micromamba R) R prints WARNING: ignoring environment value of R_HOME on stdout, which ended up in the versions.yml version strings (@ljwharbers).
  • #232 - Fixed haplotagged BAMs silently losing reads on contigs missing from the phased germline VCF header (chrM, unplaced/alt contigs, chrY without calls; #231): ClairS-TO only lists contigs with calls, and longphase haplotag only writes contigs listed in the VCF header. A new REHEADER_GERMLINE step (bcftools reheader --fai) now gives the germline VCF the full reference contig list before phasing; records are unchanged. A new small nf-test of PHASING_HAPLOTYPING with a reference contig that has reads but no germline calls covers it.
  • #219 - Fixed paired PacBio samples being dropped when only one of the tumour and normal BAMs kept its kinetics. The tumour/normal joins keyed on METAEXTRACT's per-BAM kinetics flag, so such a pair was silently left out of all variant calling, and the report join then crashed with "Invalid method invocation call". kinetics is now dropped from the meta after alignment (only the m6A branch reads it). The tumour/normal join uses failOnMismatch, so meta drift stops the run instead of dropping a pair, and a sample whose BAMs resolve to different Clair3/ClairS/ClairS-TO models, which also key those joins, now stops the run with an error naming the models (validateSampleModels). The small -stub test tests/kinetics_pairing.nf.test covers both (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #207 - Fixed FIBERTOOLSRS_PREDICTM6A crashing (range start index 4294958926 out of range for slice of length 0) on aligned BAM input with secondary alignments, which minimap2 writes by default with SEQ *. Secondary and supplementary records are now dropped before fibertools-rs (SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP), so they are no longer counted in the fibertools-rs QC either; MINIMAP2_ALIGN dropped them before realignment already. On Revio reads the m6A calls of the primary records are unchanged, and after samtools reset equal those made on the same reads unaligned (@ljwharbers).
  • #229 - The CHM13 ASCAT GC-content file (GCcontent_SNPloci_CHM13.txt.zip) is now fetched from the IntGenomicsLab Globus collection instead of GitHub. GitHub served it through Git LFS with a Last-Modified header that changes over time, so Nextflow treated it as a new file and downloaded it again on every -resume, re-running UNZIP_GC and everything that depends on it. The file content is unchanged (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #229 - --ascat_allele_files, --ascat_loci_files, --ascat_gc_file and --ascat_rt_file now override the --genome defaults as documented. nextflow.config and the schema declared ascat_gc_files/ascat_rt_files instead, which nothing read, and did not declare the allele and loci parameters at all (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #225 - PacBio tumour-only SAVANA calls are now filtered against the genome's Severus germline SV panel of normals before VEP, Padfoot and ReConPlot. SAVANA's PacBio classifier only rejects a call on matched-normal evidence, so without a normal its somatic VCF held nearly every germline SV (27,591 events on a simulated tumour-only C8, against 2 records with the matched normal) and RECONPLOT_SAVANA took 6-8 h; the filter, Severus's own PoN matching rule in bin/savana_pon_filter.py / SAVANA_PON_FILTER, removes 97% of them (761 kept), and RECONPLOT_SAVANA then finishes in 21 min with every figure drawn (unfiltered: not finished after 2 h). The 761 left are still germline by C8's matched normal, so PacBio tumour-only SAVANA calls remain a fallback. The unfiltered VCF is still published; --savana_pb_pon_filter false turns it off (@ljwharbers).
  • #225 - ReConPlot draws at most --reconplot_max_svs SVs in each of its per-chromosome, genome-wide and focus figure sets (default 1000, best supported first; a figure missing some of its SVs says top N of M SVs), since ReConPlot adds one plot layer per SV: tens of thousands take hours, and the genome-wide panel already overflows R's node stack at ~2,000 (no genome-wide figure was drawn for BL1, 2,084 SAVANA junctions, or for 2,500 capped C8 junctions; 761 drew). The harmonised *.reconplot_sv.tsv table keeps every SV (@ljwharbers).
  • #224 - Fixed CLAIR3 with --use_gpu, which failed at start with "Reference index fai file not found". The GPU image hkubal/clair3:v2.0.2_gpu follows the reference symlink and looks for the .fai next to the real file, but Nextflow stages the index from a different task. The GPU image is now hkubal/clair3:v2.0.5_gpu, which has the fix and bundles the same models. CPU runs keep the 2.0.3 biocontainer. The image doesn't run on GPUs newer than compute capability 9.0, such as the B200. docs/usage.md and the schema now say so and list every tool that --use_gpu affects (@ljwharbers).
