  • #223 - Fixed the Severus input channel (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - PREPARE_AA_DATA_REPO no longer reads a versions output UNTAR does not have, which crashed every default GRCh38 run with CoRAL; overriding --aa_data_repo_url drops the genome's default MD5 (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - -profile test_full starts again: it skips CoRAL and signatures and carries the chr19 SAVANA workarounds from test (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG no longer crashes when ASCAT finds no solution and writes an empty segments table (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - CoRAL and AmpliconClassifier tasks killed again after their last retry are ignored instead of stopping the run (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - Paired SAVANA_CNA now gets the canonical contigs file; SAVANA and ClairS-TO no longer fail on null contigs or PoN lists without --genome (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - --germline_var_keep/--somatic_var_keep are validated at launch; conda/mamba runs fail at launch when modkit, the report or signatures would run (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - SigProfiler no longer fails on samples with no SNVs; AlphaMissenseProtein reports not_found rather than aa_mismatch when the exact position is absent; MultiQC strips only the NanoStats _aln suffix (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #205 - CoRAL outputs: cycles publish to ecdna/coral/cycles, Pyomo models/ dumps are not published, SCIP gets one solver thread, the summary is named <prefix>_amplicon_summary.txt, and AmpliconClassifier's extra tables are published; docs corrected to match (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #218 - VEPPLUGIN_REVEL (and VEPPLUGIN_EVE) failed with grep: invalid option -- 'P' because the bcftools:1.24 image has a BusyBox grep; the tabix version is now read with sed, which works with both BusyBox and GNU tools (@laulambr).
  • #216 - --download_sigprofiler_genome failed on CHM13 with CHM13-T2T failed the SigProfilerMatrixGenerator checksum verification. The published payload had been replaced by the archive rebuilt after SigProfilerMatrixGenerator#251, which counts transcript-end bases correctly, while the image still carried the old checksums. The SigProfiler modules now use ghcr.io/ljwharbers/sigprofiler:1.3.6-chm13-7894689 (oras://ghcr.io/ljwharbers/sigprofiler-sif:1.3.6-chm13-7894689), and the CHM13 sigprofiler_genome_url points at the versioned chm13_release_2026-09 payload. The new SigProfilerMatrixGenerator also includes upstream's corrected GRCh38 payload, which the AlexandrovLab FTP has served as GRCh38.tar.gz since 2026-09-25; the old one is now GRCh38_Legacy. GRCh38 and CHM13-T2T volumes installed before this change fail verification and must be reinstalled. A volume passed with --sigprofiler_genome_dir is now checked once, up front, by the new SIGPROFILER_VERIFY step, which stops with reinstall instructions instead of failing in every SIGPROFILER_MATRIXGENERATOR task. Its error names the cause: missing chromosome files, a checksum mismatch (stale or corrupted payload), or a genome the image has no checksums for. Stub nf-tests (tag small) now cover PREPARE_SIGNATURES, the volume reaching every SIGPROFILER_MATRIXGENERATOR sample, and the pinned image in SIGPROFILER_MATRIXGENERATOR and SIGPROFILER_ASSIGNMENT. Transcribed-strand matrices (SBS288, SBS384) change slightly; SBS96 and the COSMIC fits are not expected to change (@ljwharbers).
  • #206 - A remote (http, https or ftp) ClinVar is now downloaded once per run by the new VEPPLUGIN_CLINVAR step in PREPARE_VEP_PLUGINS, instead of being staged by Nextflow as a foreign file; local and cloud-storage paths are staged as before. GERMLINE_VEP and SOMATIC_VEP re-checked the foreign file on its host for every sample, and NCBI answered the burst from a multi-sample GRCh38 run with HTTP 503, so SOMATIC_VEP failed with Can't stage file ...clinvar_20260829.vcf.gz; -resume could not recover, since the failed check changed the staging cache key. The download is checked against the new --vep_clinvar_md5 and --vep_clinvar_tbi_md5, set by default to the checksums NCBI (GRCh38, VCF only) and Ensembl (CHM13, VCF and index) publish, so the pinned release cannot change silently. Resuming a run that already finished re-runs GERMLINE_VEP and SOMATIC_VEP once, since ClinVar now comes from a task rather than the stage cache. The ClinVar sizes in docs/usage.md are also corrected, and docs/output.md now documents vep_plugins/ (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #203 - CLAIRS no longer runs with --haplotagged_tumor_bam_provided_so_skip_intermediate_phasing_and_haplotagging. Since somatic calling was moved ahead of PHASING_HAPLOTYPING (v1.1.0), ClairS has received the untagged minimap2 BAM, so the flag made it skip its own phasing and haplotagging and call every paired sample without haplotype information: the full-alignment model saw no HP tags and the haplotype filtering step had nothing to filter on, the same as --disable_phasing. ClairS now runs Clair3 on the normal and tumour BAMs and phases the tumour itself. Paired somatic calls change (fewer false positives expected), and CLAIRS takes longer and uses more work-directory space (@ljwharbers).
  • #203 - docs/output.md now lists the ClairS SNV output as snvs.vcf.gz, the name the pipeline publishes, instead of snv.vcf.gz (@ljwharbers).
  • #200 - *_var_combine = 'all' now keeps both callers' private calls; the prioritized caller's own private calls were previously dropped. Invalid combine_method/prioritize_caller values now raise an error (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #200 - *_var_combine = 'consensus' now splits multi-allelic records before intersecting, so they match across callers, and rejoins them before phasing. 'all' now keeps the prioritised caller's record wherever both callers call a position, so no record mixes two callers' alleles (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #200 - With --smallvar_filter_pass false, 'all' now prefers a PASS record over a non-PASS one at each position before applying the caller priority, so a prioritised caller's RefCall/LowQual record no longer drops the other caller's PASS call. It also keeps one record where left-alignment moves two of one caller's indels onto the same position (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #200 - Somatic phasing no longer includes germline records at the position of an alt-genotype somatic call, which gave the somatic record the germline genotype and phase set (new BCFTOOLS_EXCLUDE_SITES module); 0/0 and ./. somatic records are published unphased (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #200 - LRSOMATICREPORT now renders each sample as soon as its own inputs are ready instead of waiting for the whole batch, including samples without ASCAT's optional raw segments output (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #200 - Bumped WAKHAN from 0.4.3 to 0.4.4, fixing a deterministic StatisticsError crash in BAF binning that aborted the run (@robert-a-forsyth).
  • #196 - LRSOMATICREPORT now points XDG_CACHE_HOME at the task directory alongside HOME and TMPDIR. Singularity/Apptainer inherit the host environment, so on sites that set it outside the bind-mounted work tree the render died with Read-only file system (os error 30): mkdir '<...>/.cache/quarto' (@AmberVerhasselt, @ljwharbers).
  • #193 - --vep_eve https://evemodel.org/api/proteins/bulk/download/ was rejected at launch because the "needs preparing" check keyed on a .zip suffix; it now checks whether the value is already a prepared bgzipped file (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #188 - MODKIT_PILEUP now runs a patched modkit 0.6.4 (ljwharbers/modkit@pacbio-conflict-fix): ghcr.io/ljwharbers/modkit:0.6.4-pacbiofix-6e0afa2 under Docker and oras://ghcr.io/ljwharbers/modkit-sif:0.6.4-pacbiofix-6e0afa2 under Singularity/Apptainer. Stock modkit 0.4.3-0.6.4 dropped 32-65 % of reads from recent PacBio HiFi BAMs and returned empty --cpg pileups (nanoporetech/modkit#612, fix proposed in nanoporetech/modkit#720), and ignored --phased/--modified-bases for PacBio BAMs with 6mA calls. The image is linux/amd64 only and Conda is not supported (use --skip_modkit there); return to the biocontainer once a release includes the fix (@ljwharbers).
  • #181 - NanoPlot pre- and post-alignment statistics now reach MultiQC; their channels were declared but never assigned, so the NanoStat section was silently missing from every report (@ljwharbers).
  • #181 - NANOPLOT_PRE now includes the replicate in its output prefix, so samples with more than one replicate no longer collapse into a single MultiQC sample (@ljwharbers).
  • #181 - samtools stats/flagstat/idxstats and mosdepth outputs are now prefixed <sample>_<type> instead of <sample>; the tumor and normal files of a matched pair shared a basename, so MultiQC logged Duplicate sample name found! Overwriting and reported only one of them (@ljwharbers).
  • #194 - A sample whose clair3_model differs from the model implied by its BAM header no longer makes Clair3 run twice on every normal BAM sharing that header model, with a random copy winning the downstream join. The same bug made UNTAR fail with mkdir: missing operand when the header's basecall model was absent from the model map (#191). Model entries are now keyed on the downloaded model (@YannVRB, @ljwharbers).
  • #181 - Raised MultiQC's log_filesize_limit to 500 MB, because long-read samtools stats output exceeds the 50 MB default and was silently skipped (@ljwharbers).
  • #186 - The clair_only nf-test now asserts sample4's merged tumour BAM with bam().getReadsMD5() instead of file md5s, which samtools merge makes irreproducible by giving colliding @PG IDs a random suffix (@ljwharbers).
  • #182 - Added --vcf to the default vep_args so VEP writes VCF output rather than its default tab-delimited format (@AmberVerhasselt).
  • #183 - Corrected the github URL for Laurens Lambrechts in manifest.contributors, which was a copy of @MariosEft97's, to @laulambr. RO-Crate metadata updated to match (@ljwharbers).

The callers follow the new module interfaces: .tbi/.csi/.bai outputs are now one .index channel, WGET takes the file suffix in its input tuple, and most modules report versions through the versions topic. The variant callers (Clair3, ClairS, DeepVariant, DeepSomatic) are updated in a separate PR (@ljwharbers).
Tool Old New Notes bcftools 1.20 / 1.22 1.24 All nf-core and local bcftools modules, VCFSPLIT, VEPPLUGIN_EVE/VEPPLUGIN_REVEL. BCFTOOLS_NORM now runs with --check-ref w: 1.24 aborts when a REF differs from the FASTA, and Clair3 writes N where GRCh38 has IUPAC codes (e.g. B at chr3:16902883), which 1.22 accepted samtools 1.21 / 1.22.1 / 1.23.1 1.24 Including METAEXTRACT; minimap2/align stays on nf-core's samtools 1.23.1 minimap2 2.29 2.30 2.31 has no minimap2 + samtools image yet mosdepth 0.3.11 0.3.14 nanoplot 1.46.1 1.48.0 ensembl-vep 115.2 116.1 116.2's biocontainer lacks Math::CDF; the default --vep_cache_version (113) is unchanged severus 1.6 1.7 cramino 1.3.0 2.0.0 N50, N75, median and mean read length now use the full read length (primary alignments, clipped bases included), so the report's N50 goes up; the old aligned values are new ... aligned rows. % from total alignments is renamed % from total reads fibertools-rs 0.8.1 0.13.1 Fiber-seq BAMs now carry nucleosomes, MSPs and FIREs in the MolecularAnnotation tags Ma (nuc, msp and fire intervals) and Aq (their qualities) instead of ns/nl/as/al/aq; downstream tools reading the old tags need ft convert-tags or an update wakhan 0.4.3 0.4.4 0.5.0 changes the output directory layout and has no biocontainer yet
  • #213 - Updated the small variant callers. Germline and somatic calls change with the new models (@ljwharbers).
Tool Old New Notes clair3 1.2.0 2.0.3 Clair3 v2 runs on PyTorch and cannot read the v1 TensorFlow models the pipeline downloaded from ONT's CDN. Models bundled with the image (HKU's and ONT's recent R10.4.1 SUP/HAC ones, hifi_revio) are now used from the image with no download; other models are fetched as PyTorch directories from HKU (ONT's Rerio catalogue for r9/r10 names) by the new CLAIR3_MODEL step, which replaces WGET/UNTAR and, unlike WGET, checks the TLS certificate (Clair3 unpickles the files). The GPU image is hkubal/clair3:v2.0.5_gpu (was v2.0.2_gpu until #224; see Fixed) clairs 0.4.4 0.5.1 Bundles Clair3 2.0.3 for its germline step deepvariant 1.9.0 1.10.0 nf-core update; make_examples now takes its flags from the model (--checkpoint): the ONT model is 199 wide with the new fuzzy channel, and both models call easy sites with the small model deepsomatic 1.7.0 1.10.0 make_examples_somatic now takes its flags from the model (--checkpoint) instead of a hard-coded channel list and pileup width; the paired PacBio model is 147 wide with 9 channels. The small model is kept off explicitly (--nocall_small_model_examples), because the module does not pass its calls on
  • #214 - Updated Wakhan from 0.4.4 to 0.5.0, run from docker.io/ljwharbers/wakhan:0.5.0-histfix-1afd44d (oras://docker.io/ljwharbers/wakhan-sif:0.5.0-histfix-1afd44d for Singularity/Apptainer) because no biocontainer was built for it. The image carries upstream commit 1afd44d4, which fixes the IndexError in update_coverage_hist that killed WAKHAN on some samples (KolmogorovLab/Wakhan#64). The wakhan/ output layout changes: each solution is now solution_{ploidy}_{purity}_{confidence}/ with integer_profile.{bed,vcf,html,pdf} (one boundary-aligned table for both haplotypes, replacing the two *_HP_{1,2}.bed files), subclonal_profile.*, genes/genes_copynumber_states.* and a HiScanner_plots_data.zip for the Wakhan web viewer; ranked solutions are solution_rank_{n}. Wakhan 0.5.0 no longer writes the per-chromosome variation_plots, genome_copynumbers_details plots or per-solution loh_regions*.bed. LRSOMATICREPORT now runs lrsomatic_report v1.6.1 (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report:1.6.1), which finds the copy-number plots in both layouts; v1.6.0 silently dropped them for 0.5.0 output. On CHM13 the pipeline distributes an adaptation: the protein-space release re-keyed from UniProt accession to gene symbol, split into reference/position/alternate amino-acid columns, deduplicated and tabix-indexed; rows without a gene symbol are dropped and no score is altered. File Description {tumor,normal}/modkit_pileup/sample.bed.gz Modkit pileup bedMethyl table (bgzip) with per-strand methylation frequency and coverage. By default (--modkit_args '--cpg --modified-bases 5mC') rows are 5mC calls at CpG sites only. {tumor,normal}/modkit_pileup/sample_{hp1,hp2}.bed.gz With --modkit_phased: bedMethyl tables restricted to reads carrying haplotype tag HP:1 or HP:2 from the Longphase-haplotagged BAM. {tumor,normal}/modkit_pileup/sample_combined.bed.gz With --modkit_phased: bedMethyl table over all reads, including untagged ones (equivalent to the unphased default output). There is no separate file for untagged reads; they only contribute to _combined.

With --modkit_phased set (and --skip_dmr not set), haplotype differential methylation region (DMR) calling also runs, comparing the _hp1/_hp2 bedMethyl pileups over CpG islands covered in both haplotypes and annotating each result with its nearest gene:

├── methylation
│   ├── tumor
│   │   ├── modkit_pileup
│   │   │   └── ...
│   │   └── dmr
│   │       ├── sample.log                   # modkit dmr pair's debug log
│   │       └── sample.nearestGene.bed       # final DMR deliverable
│   ├── normal                               # paired samples only
│   │   └── ...                              # same layout as tumor
File Description {tumor,normal}/dmr/sample.log modkit dmr pair's own debug log, published for troubleshooting (e.g. the invalid-bedmethyl-data class of failure) without needing -resume. The intermediate raw modkit dmr pair BED is not published, since this file supersedes it. {tumor,normal}/dmr/sample.nearestGene.bed Each modkit dmr pair DMR call (17 columns — chrom/start/end, haplotype-vs-haplotype methylation counts/fractions and the difference score; see modkit dmr pair --help for the full column list), joined via bedtools closest -D b -t first to its nearest gene from --dmr_gencode_gene_bed (that gene's own BED6: chrom/start/end/name/score/strand), followed by the signed distance to that gene (relative to the gene's own strand; negative means upstream).

DMR runs modkit dmr pair --base C, which counts every modification on C as modified. The pileup feeding it requests both 5mC and 5hmC (see --modkit_args in the usage docs), so the methylation fractions and the difference score describe 5mC and 5hmC combined, not 5mC alone.

docs.title: ecdna
docs.text:
Extrachromosomal DNA and focal amplification. CoRAL reconstructs amplicon structures from the tumour BAM, seeded by ASCAT's copy-number segments, and AmpliconClassifier labels each reconstructed amplicon (ecDNA, BFB, linear, and so on). Runs on every tumour sample with ASCAT calls; disable with --skip_coral, or keep reconstruction and drop classification with --skip_ampliconclassifier.

A sample with no segment above --coral_gain produces an empty seed BED and is skipped with a log message rather than failing. CoRAL defaults to the open-source SCIP solver; --coral_solver gurobi_direct is faster but needs --gurobi_license. AmpliconClassifier needs an AmpliconArchitect data repository, downloaded automatically for GRCh38 and supplied with --aa_data_repo for CHM13; a CHM13 run without one skips classification with a warning. An unseeded sample gets only its seed BED: no reconstruct/ directory, and so no amplicon summary.

With --coral_run_cycle, reconstruction builds the breakpoint graphs only, and the cycles and the amplicon summary are written to cycles/ instead, beside copies of the graphs; the classifier and the plots then read cycles/.

docs.title: savana
docs.text:
SAVANA structural variant and copy-number calling. Runs alongside Severus/ASCAT rather than replacing either. Matched tumor/normal samples run savana run + savana classify + savana cna as separate steps; tumor-only samples run the combined savana to command instead, producing the same file set in one step. We strongly recommend matched tumor/normal mode for best performance -- SAVANA's own docs note tumor-only calling is a fallback, best combined with population/panel-of-normals filtering.

SAVANA's PacBio classifier (--pb) has no tumour-only mode: it rejects a call only on matched-normal evidence, so a PacBio tumour-only sample.classified.somatic.vcf holds nearly every germline SV in the genome (~28k on a 30x sample). For these samples the pipeline removes the SVs found in the genome's Severus germline SV panel of normals (Severus's matching rule) and passes sample.pon_filtered.classified.somatic.vcf to VEP, Padfoot and ReConPlot instead; about 97% of the calls are removed. What remains is still mostly germline (on a PacBio pair, all 761 survivors had matched-normal support), so treat PacBio tumour-only SAVANA SVs as a fallback and prefer Severus or a matched normal. Turn this off with --savana_pb_pon_filter false.

The germline and somatic VCFs carry these extra subfields inside VEP's CSQ INFO annotation, on top of what --everything already produces; the SV VCF is annotated without plugins. Read them out with bcftools +split-vep.

Field Source Appears on am_pathogenicity, am_class AlphaMissense plugin GRCh38 AlphaMissenseProtein_match AlphaMissenseProtein CHM13 am_pathogenicity, am_class AlphaMissenseProtein CHM13, when the lookup resolves SIFT_score, SIFT_pred PolyPhen_SIFT plugin CHM13 (GRCh38 gets SIFT from cache) PolyPhen_humvar_score, PolyPhen_humvar_pred PolyPhen_SIFT plugin CHM13, as above ClinVar_CLNSIG, ClinVar_CLNREVSTAT, ClinVar_CLNDN ClinVar --custom both, fields set by --vep_clinvar_fields REVEL REVEL plugin GRCh38 CADD_PHRED, CADD_RAW CADD plugin GRCh38, only with --vep_cadd_snv / --vep_cadd_indel EVE_SCORE, EVE_CLASS EVE plugin GRCh38, only with --vep_eve

AlphaMissenseProtein_match records how the CHM13 protein-space lookup resolved, and is the field to check before trusting — or explaining — a missing score:

Value Meaning gene_aa Matched on gene symbol and both amino acids; am_pathogenicity is populated aa_mismatch The gene and position exist, but the reference amino acid differs — the CHM13 protein and the one AlphaMissense was numbered against disagree here, so no score is given not_found No row for this gene, position and substitution no_gene VEP produced no gene symbol for the transcript, so no lookup was possible

Only missense substitutions are looked up at all; anything else carries no AlphaMissenseProtein_* field rather than a match value.

File Description sample.shatterseek.tsv One row per chromosome (chr1-22, chrX): the largest cluster of interleaved SVs, the statistical criteria and the confidence tiers sample.shatterseek_{sv,cn}_input.tsv The SV and copy-number tables exactly as given to ShatterSeek (Ensembl chromosome names, integer copy number) plots/*.pdf ShatterSeek figure (ideogram, SVs, copy number, summary) for every chromosome with a confidence tier (optional) shatterseek.log Wrapper log: files read, SVs dropped and why, copy numbers rounded, the tiers called

ShatterSeek (Cortes-Ciriano et al. 2020) finds, per chromosome, the largest cluster of interleaved intra-chromosomal SVs and tests it against the hallmarks of chromothripsis. The pipeline runs upstream ShatterSeek (v1.1, pinned commit) unchanged, apart from a build-time patch adding T2T-CHM13 chromosome sizes and cytobands. The columns are upstream's:

Column Meaning start, end Span of the chromosome's largest cluster of interleaved intra-chromosomal SVs (NA without one) number_DEL/_DUP/_h2hINV/_t2tINV The cluster's SVs by type number_TRA, clusterSize_including_TRA Translocations with a breakend inside the cluster, and the cluster size including them pval_fragment_joins Chi-square test of the cluster's SV types (translocations typed by strand) against equal proportions; chromothripsis should not be significant chr_breakpoint_enrichment Binomial test of the translocations touching this chromosome against its share of the genome pval_exp_chr, pval_exp_cluster Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests of the breakpoints (chromosome / cluster) against an exponential distribution; significant = clustered breakpoints max_number_oscillating_CN_segments_2_states Longest run of adjacent copy-number segments in the cluster region alternating between two states q_* Benjamini-Hochberg q-values of the four tests across the sample's chromosomes (added by the wrapper) inter_* Other chromosomes linked to this one by translocations, and the fragment-joins test over the linked clusters HC1, HC2, HC3 PCAWG high-confidence tiers met (see below) chromothripsis_criteria, chromothripsis_confidence The tiers met, e.g. HC1,HC2, and high (any tier) or none

The tiers use the PCAWG high-confidence cut-offs (Cortes-Ciriano et al. 2020, Supplementary Note 1.2; ShatterSeek issue #22), with significance at q ≤ 0.2 and NA counting as a fail. Interleaved intra SVs is the sum of the four SV-type columns. PCAWG's low-confidence tier (4-6 oscillating segments) is not reported.

Tier Interleaved intra SVs Other Oscillating CN segments (2 states) Fragment joins Enrichment or exp_chr test HC1 ≥ 6 ≥ 7 q > 0.2 q ≤ 0.2 HC2 ≥ 3 ≥ 4 translocations ≥ 7 q > 0.2 HC3 ≥ 40 SVs incl. translocations q > 0.2

Points to keep in mind when reading the calls:

  • PCAWG applied HC3 only to osteosarcomas, leiomyosarcomas and liposarcomas, where amplification erodes the oscillating pattern; here it applies to every tumour. Drop it with ext.args = '--no-hc3'.
  • PCAWG corrected the P values once across every chromosome of all 2,658 tumours; within one sample the correction covers 23 chromosomes. The raw P values are kept, so a cohort-wide correction can be recomputed from the summaries (each row carries sample, cn_source and sv_source).
  • Upstream's exponential tests compare against random draws; the wrapper seeds R's generator (--seed, default 1), so a rerun gives the same P values. Clusters of equal size are pooled before the statistics are computed, so a chromosome whose SVs are all singletons is summarised over all of them.
  • The cut-offs were set by visual inspection of PCAWG's short-read consensus calls. Long-read callers report many small SVs, whose two breakpoints a few hundred bp apart make the exponential test significant on most chromosomes; intra-chromosomal SVs shorter than --shatterseek_min_svlen (default 150 bp) are therefore left out, and raising it tests larger rearrangements only.
  • ShatterSeek does not mask centromeres or satellite arrays. A cluster spanning a centromere or heterochromatin block (e.g. chr16 q11.2, chr1 q12, chr9 q12) is more likely mapping artefact than chromothripsis; check the figure.
  • Tumour-only Severus calls include germline SVs that the panel of normals did not remove.
  • Insertions and single breakends are not used, nor are SVs touching chrY, the mitochondrion or unplaced contigs. SAVANA's absolute copy number and fractional Wakhan states are rounded to integers, and neighbouring segments with equal copy number are merged, because ShatterSeek counts copy-number states row by row.

Tier cut-offs, the q/P choice and SV filters can be changed with ext.args on .*:SHATTERSEEK_(SEVERUS_ASCAT|SEVERUS_WAKHAN|SAVANA) (see Rscript assets/shatterseek/run_shatterseek.R --help). A sample ShatterSeek cannot process is skipped without stopping the run.

docs.text:
Output files 
├── report
│   ├── {sample}_report.html
│   ├── {sample}_small_variants.tsv.gz
File Description {sample}_report.html Self-contained per-sample HTML report (lrsomatic_report, run from ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report): clinical overview, circos plot, small/structural variant tables, copy number, genomic instability, signatures and QC. Any section whose upstream data is unavailable (e.g. a skipped tool) shows a "not available" notice instead. {sample}_small_variants.tsv.gz The full small-variant table behind the report's variant section, every row and column, as gzipped TSV. Written when the somatic VEP file holds at least one variant: not with --skip_vep, and not for a sample with no somatic calls. The HTML may embed only part of it (see --embed in usage); this file is always complete.

This is the final step of the pipeline, run after every tool it reads. It renders each sample only once the run's last SigProfiler, ShatterSeek, ecDNA, SAVANA, Padfoot, ReConPlot and Wakhan output has been written, because several of those are optional per sample. Disable it with --skip_report.

The report reads these published outputs of the sample (a skipped tool's section shows a notice):

Report section Files read Small variants vep/somatic/{sample}_SOMATIC_VEP.vcf.gz, variants/phased/ somatic VCF, variants/clairsto/{sample}.verdict_status.tsv (tumour-only) Structural variants variants/severus/somatic_SVs/severus_somatic.vcf.gz, vep/SVs/{sample}_SV_VEP.vcf.gz; SAVANA's variants/savana/{sample}[.pon_filtered].classified.somatic.vcf (PoN-filtered for PacBio tumour-only) and vep/SVs/{sample}_VEP_SAVANA.vcf.gz SV annotation and figures padfoot/{pair}/{annotated_svs,by_gene}.tsv, reconplot/{pair}/{genome_wide,per_chromosome,focus}/*.png Copy number ascat/{sample}.{purityploidy,segments_raw,metrics}.txt and plots, variants/savana/{sample}_fitted_purity_ploidy.tsv, wakhan/solutions_ranks.tsv, wakhan/solution_rank_1/{integer_profile.bed,genes/genes_copynumber_states.bed} Chromothripsis shatterseek/{pair}/{sample}.shatterseek.tsv ecDNA ecdna/amplicon_classifier/{sample}_{amplicon_classification_profiles,gene_list,result_table}.tsv, ecdna/coral/{sample}_CNV_SEEDS.bed, ecdna/coral/{reconstruct,cycles}/{sample}_amplicon_summary.txt, ecdna/coral/plots/*_{graph,cycles}.png Mutational signatures signatures/assignment/COSMIC_v*/{SBS96,DBS78,ID83}/Assignment_Solution/{Activities,Solution_Stats}/, signatures/matrices/output/{SBS,DBS,ID}/*.{SBS96,DBS78,ID83}.all QC and phasing mosdepth, cramino and samtools files under qc/{tumor,normal}/, qc/whatshap_stats/{sample}_whatshap_stats.tsv HMF driver annotation The genome's hosted HMF bundle (GRCh38, CHM13; unpacked copy published under cache/hmf/hmf_report_<genome>/) or your own --report_hmf_* resources (usage), plus the small-variant, SV and copy-number files above

The pipeline passes each sample's run mode, --run-mode paired for a tumour/normal pair and --run-mode tumour_only otherwise, which sets the report's header badge and its tumour-only caveat; the report no longer guesses it from the staged QC files.

Wakhan's interactive HTML plots (wakhan/solution_*/integer_profile.html, the subclonal profiles and {sample}_heatmap_ploidy_purity.html) are no longer embedded in the report, which draws the top-ranked solution's copy-number profile from integer_profile.bed instead; open them from the wakhan directory.

Sections:

  • Small variants — the VEP-annotated somatic SNVs/indels, with VAF, depth and phase set from the phased somatic VCF; a footnote names the file those columns came from and, after a consensus run, notes that a multi-caller variant's VAF comes from whichever caller won the merge. Unfiltered by default; see --report_gene_panel in usage.
  • Pathogenicity predictors (SIFT, PolyPhen, AlphaMissense, ClinVar, CADD, REVEL, EVE) are read from the plugin fields in CSQ, each as a class column with a tickbox filter and a numeric score column. A column appears only when the annotated VCF declared that field, and an Annotation sources footnote lists which sources were present.
  • Structural variants — SEVERUS breakpoints, annotated from the VEP SV VCF ({sample}_SV_VEP.vcf.gz), one row per rearrangement. Breakends additionally get their own circos plot, cross-linked to the SV table and redrawn as the table is filtered. Skipping VEP leaves the SV table unannotated but still drawn on the circos plot.
  • Circos — genome-wide SNV density, SVs and copy number, with the tier 1–2 key-finding genes of the ticked gene list(s) labelled around the outside; the labels follow the panel checkboxes, so with no list ticked there are none.
  • ReConPlot figures — by default (the report's --embed slim) no genome-wide strip, and per-chromosome figures only for chromosomes with a ShatterSeek chromothripsis call, an SV with a Padfoot HIGH_ONCO/HIGH_TSG rating, or a tier 1–2 SV or copy-number key finding of a ticked gene list. The report option --embed full (usage) embeds every figure; all of them remain under reconplot.
  • Copy number — ASCAT purity/ploidy, whole-genome doubling and LOH (from metrics.txt) plus its diagnostic plots, SAVANA's fitted purity/ploidy, and, when WAKHAN ran, its ranked purity/ploidy solutions with the top-ranked solution's copy-number profile and gene copy-number states.
  • HMF driver annotation — on by default for GRCh38 and CHM13 (--skip_report_hmf turns it off), from the genome's hosted bundle or your own resources (usage): Hartwig's driver panel, hotspots and known fusions applied to the small variants (reported per the panel's flags, on the canonical transcript), to ASCAT and Wakhan copy number separately plus Severus/SAVANA deletions (amplifications and deletions, with a per-source on/off switch), and to the SV breakends (known fusions with exon ranges and frame). The driver panel is also added to the gene-list checkboxes as hmf_driver. Absent otherwise.
  • QC — mosdepth, cramino and samtools statistics; for a matched tumour/normal pair both sides are shown side by side. A collapsible Phasing block shows the per-chromosome WhatsHap statistics of the phased germline VCF (the normal's in a pair, the tumour's in tumour-only mode), and the header's "Phased variants" card their genome-wide total; both are absent with --skip_whatshapstats or --skip_qc.

Filtering in the browser:

  • Gene panels are checkboxes in the panel bar; ticked panels are unioned, and --report_gene_panel only sets which are ticked on load — see usage. With two or more ticked, each panel_hit entry names the panel it matched in square brackets.
  • Categorical columns filter by tickbox dropdown rather than a text box: consequence, impact and callers on the small-variant table, and svclass, svtype, impact, consequence and caller on the SV table. Each dropdown lists the values actually present in that sample with a row count. Ticking several values in one column is OR; ticking values in two columns is AND. A column with fewer than two distinct values keeps a plain text box. Every other column keeps its text box, and the table's own search box still does substring across all columns.

The report is one self-contained file — plots and tables are embedded, so it can be copied or emailed on its own.

--download_sigprofiler_genomeboolean true Download and install the ~3 GB SigProfilerMatrixGenerator genome payload during the run when no --sigprofiler_genome_dir is given. --sigprofiler_cosmic_versionnumber 3.6 COSMIC reference signature version fitted by SigProfilerAssignment. --sigprofiler_exclude_signature_subgroupsstring - Comma-separated SigProfilerAssignment signature subgroups to exclude from the fit (e.g. `Artifact_signatures,Lymphoid_signatures`). --sigprofiler_matrix_argsstring --plot Extra arguments for `SigProfilerMatrixGenerator matrix_generator` (e.g. `--plot --tsb_stat`). `--bed_file`, `--exome` and `--seqInfo False` are not supported. --sigprofiler_assignment_argsstring - Extra arguments for `SigProfilerAssignment cosmic_fit` (e.g. `--make_plots False`). Report options

Options for the final per-sample HTML report

ParameterDefaultDescription --report_gene_panelstring - Gene panel(s) applied when the report opens, as a comma-separated list: 'none' for no filtering, builtin panel names (e.g. 'lymphoid'), and/or paths to TSVs with a 'gene' column. Several panels are unioned; default (unset) is unfiltered.More info

Every builtin panel is embedded in the report as a checkbox, so this only sets the initial selection. An entry is read as a panel file if it contains a '/' or ends in '.tsv', and as a builtin panel name otherwise. 'none' cannot be combined with a real panel, and two panel files sharing a base name cannot be combined.

--report_hmf_resource_dirstring - Root of a Hartwig (oncoanalyser) GRCh38 resource bundle, lifted over on --genome CHM13 (or a copy the pipeline already lifted). Turns on the report's optional HMF driver annotation, taking its files from the bundle's standard layout.directory-pathMore info

Reads common/DriverGenePanel.38.tsv, common/ensembl_data/, dna/sv/known_fusion_data.38.csv, dna/variants/KnownHotspots.somatic.38.vcf.gz and dna/variants/ActionableCodingPanel.38.bed(.gz) (absent from bundle v3, then skipped). Any --report_hmf_* file parameter overrides its file. The bundle is GRCh38: on --genome CHM13 it is lifted over first (HMF_LIFTOVER, see --report_hmf_liftover_chain), or a copy the pipeline already lifted (its common/ensembl_data/REFERENCE says t2t) is used as is; such a copy is rejected on GRCh38. With any other --genome, or on CHM13 when no chain resolves, the annotation is skipped with a warning. The bundle is not distributed with the pipeline; download it from the oncoanalyser documentation.

--report_hmf_driver_panelstring - HMF DriverGenePanel.38.tsv. Turns on the report's HMF driver annotation (with --report_hmf_ensembl_data_dir) and adds the panel as the selectable gene list 'hmf_driver'.file-path --report_hmf_ensembl_data_dirstring - HMF Ensembl data cache directory (the bundle's common/ensembl_data, with ensembl_gene_data.csv and ensembl_trans_exon_data.csv). Required for the HMF driver annotation.directory-path --report_hmf_known_fusionsstring - HMF known_fusion_data.38.csv: known-fusion matching of the SV calls in the report's HMF section (optional).file-path --report_hmf_hotspotsstring - HMF KnownHotspots.somatic.38.vcf.gz: hotspot matching of small variants in the report's HMF section (optional).file-path --report_hmf_liftover_chainstring - GRCh38 -> CHM13 chain file used to lift the HMF resources over on a CHM13 run. Default: the genome's (the T2T consortium's grch38-chm13v2.chain).file-pathMore info

On --genome CHM13 the pipeline lifts the GRCh38 HMF resources over to CHM13 (HMF_LIFTOVER) before the report: the Ensembl data cache (a transcript is kept only if every exon lifts whole), hotspots (REF re-checked against the CHM13 FASTA), the actionable coding panel and the known fusions' IG/enhancer ranges. The lifted bundle is published under pipeline_info/hmf_liftover/ and can be given back as --report_hmf_resource_dir. The default chain is the T2T consortium's (public domain), downloaded at launch (~6 MB); offline, download it once and pass its local path here, or reuse a lifted bundle. A chain that cannot be reached is an error at launch.

--report_hmf_actionable_bedstring - HMF ActionableCodingPanel.38.bed(.gz): flags small variants in its regions in the report's HMF section (optional; a calling-sensitivity region set, not an actionability call).file-path CoRAL / ecDNA options

Amplicon reconstruction with CoRAL and classification with AmpliconClassifier.

ParameterDefaultDescription --coral_gainnumber 6.0 Minimum total copy number for a segment to seed an amplicon (CoRAL's --gain). --coral_min_seed_sizeinteger 100000 Minimum seed interval size in bp (CoRAL's --min-seed-size). --coral_max_seg_gapinteger 300000 Largest gap in bp that CoRAL will bridge when merging seed segments (--max-seg-gap). --coral_solverstring scip Optimiser for CoRAL's non-convex MIQCP cycle decomposition. SCIP is open-source and needs no licence; gurobi_direct is faster but requires --gurobi_license.Options: scip gurobi_direct --coral_solver_time_limitinteger 7200 Per-amplicon solver time limit in seconds (CoRAL's --solver-time-limit). --coral_global_time_limitinteger 21600 Per-sample time limit in seconds across all amplicons (CoRAL's --global-time-limit). --coral_min_bp_supportnumber 1.75 Minimum breakpoint read support (CoRAL's --min-bp-support). CoRAL's own README recommends a much larger value such as 10.0 for WGS; 1.75 matches the setting validated on this cohort. --coral_run_cycleboolean - Decompose cycles in a separate `coral cycle_all` step: reconstruction then builds the breakpoint graphs only (CoRAL's --skip-cycle-decomp). --coral_cycle_decomp_alphanumber 0.01 Cycle decomposition alpha, balancing copy-number weight against path constraints: CoRAL reconstruct's --cycle-decomp-alpha, or cycle_all's --alpha with --coral_run_cycle. --coral_plotboolean true Render CoRAL's per-amplicon graph and cycle plots. Plot failures never fail the run. --gurobi_licensestring - Path to a gurobi.lic, mounted into the CoRAL tasks. Required with --coral_solver gurobi_direct.file-path --aa_data_repostring - AmpliconArchitect data repository for AmpliconClassifier: the directory holding `GRCh38/` or `CHM13/`, or that reference directory itself. Downloaded automatically for GRCh38; CHM13 has no published repo, so without one the classifier is skipped with a warning.directory-pathMore info

Downloading the GRCh38 repo fetches 1.1 GB and unpacks about 4 GB on every run. Extract `GRCh38.tar.gz` once and pass the directory here to skip both.

--aa_data_repo_md5string - Expected MD5 of the downloaded AmpliconArchitect data repository tarball.More info

The GRCh38 default carries the MD5 the host publishes, and a tarball that does not match fails the run, so the repository cannot change silently. A local --aa_data_repo takes no MD5, and setting --aa_data_repo drops the default.

Skip options

Define whether to skip certain steps

ParameterDefaultDescription --skip_qcboolean - Skips all QC steps --skip_craminoboolean - Skips Cramino --skip_signaturesboolean - Skips mutational signature analysis (SigProfilerMatrixGenerator + SigProfilerAssignment) --skip_mosdepthboolean - Skips Mosdepth --skip_bamstatsboolean - Skips samtools flagstat, stats, and idxstats --skip_wakhanboolean - Skips wakhan --skip_modkitboolean - Skip the modkit pileup of base modifications. --skip_fiberboolean - Skip Fibertools steps --skip_ascatboolean - Skip ASCAT. ClairS-TO's Verdict germline tagging of tumour-only calls then uses Verdict's own purity and copy number estimate instead of ASCAT's. Either way Verdict tags nothing when the purity is above 0.6. --skip_savanaboolean - Skip SAVANA (SV + copy-number calling) --skip_dmrboolean - Skip differential methylation region (DMR) calling between haplotypes. Only takes effect when --modkit_phased is also set; has no effect otherwise. --skip_padfootboolean - Skips Padfoot SV/CNA annotationMore info

Skips Padfoot annotation of somatic SVs and CNAs (Severus + Wakhan and SAVANA pairs). Padfoot runs only inside its container; skip it under `-profile conda`.

--skip_reconplotboolean - Skips ReConPlot SV/CNA figuresMore info

Skips the ReConPlot rearrangement and copy-number figures (ASCAT + Severus, Wakhan + Severus and SAVANA pairs). ReConPlot runs only inside its container; skip it under `-profile conda`.

--skip_shatterseekboolean - Skips ShatterSeek chromothripsis callingMore info

Skips ShatterSeek chromothripsis calling (ASCAT + Severus, Wakhan + Severus and SAVANA pairs). ShatterSeek runs only inside its container; skip it under `-profile conda`.

--skip_m6aboolean - Skip m6a calling by FibertoolsMore info

For PacBio fiber-seq reads that already carry m6A calls (m6A is only predicted from PacBio kinetics; ONT reads carry the calls of their basecaller). A fiber-seq file whose first 1000 reads carry no m6A calls (no A+a entry in their MM tags) and gets none predicted skips the nucleosome, FIRE and fibertools-rs QC steps, with a warning naming the sample, with or without this option.

--skip_vepboolean - Skip VEP annotation --skip_vep_pluginsboolean - Skip the VEP plugin annotation, keeping the rest of VEPMore info

Annotate with VEP alone, downloading no plugin data. Plugins are on by default on --genome GRCh38 (about 1.4 GB on a first run) and --genome CHM13 (about 14 GB, mostly the pangenome PolyPhen/SIFT database); CADD and EVE are opt-in. --igenomes_ignore and a non-human --genome also leave the plugins off.

--skip_normalfiberboolean - Skip Fibertools steps for the normal sample --skip_nanoplotboolean - Skip Nanoplot --skip_whatshapstatsboolean - Skip WhatsHap stats --skip_modcallboolean - Skip Longphase `modcall`, the 5mC base-modification calling whose VCF is used as extra evidence during phasing. Unrelated to the modkit pileup (see `skip_modkit`). --use_gpuboolean - Run DeepVariant/DeepSomatic call_variants and Clair3 on a GPU (use with the gpu profile).More info

Only DEEPVARIANT_CALLVARIANTS, DEEPSOMATIC_CALLVARIANTS and CLAIR3 use a GPU; every other step, fibertools-rs included, runs on the CPU either way. The DeepVariant/DeepSomatic 1.10.0-gpu images (TensorFlow 2.16.1, CUDA 12.3) and Clair3's GPU image support NVIDIA GPUs up to the Hopper generation (compute capability 9.0 or lower, e.g. A100, H100); on Blackwell cards such as the B200 (compute capability 10.0) call_variants fails with CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PTX and Clair3 fails too, so leave this off there.

--skip_reportboolean - Skip the final per-sample HTML report --skip_report_hmfboolean - Skip the report's HMF driver annotation (on by default for GRCh38 and CHM13).More info

By default the report's HMF driver annotation uses the genome's hosted bundle (GRCh38, or CHM13 lifted over; about 5 MB, downloaded once per run and MD5-checked). Your own resources via --report_hmf_resource_dir or the --report_hmf_* files take over from it. Other genomes have no bundle and run without the annotation.

--skip_coralboolean - Skip CoRAL amplicon reconstruction and AmpliconClassifier. --skip_ampliconclassifierboolean - Run CoRAL but skip AmpliconClassifier, which avoids needing an AA data repository. Generic options

Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.

ParameterDefaultDescription --multiqc_methods_descriptionstring - Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description. --helpboolean - Display the help message. --help_fullboolean - Display the full detailed help message. --show_hiddenboolean - Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided). Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

--igenomes_basestring s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes/ The base path to the igenomes reference files Institutional config options
