docs.title: IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic: Usage
docs.text: Documentation of pipeline parameters is generated automatically from the pipeline schema and can no longer be found in markdown files.

docs.title: Samplesheet input
docs.text:
You will need to create a samplesheet with information about the samples you would like to analyse before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file of the following form:

sample,bam_tumor,bam_normal,platform,sex,fiber
sample1,tumour.bam,normal.bam,ont,female,n
sample2,tumour.bam,,ont,female,y
sample3,tumour.bam,,pb,male,n
sample4,tumour.bam,normal.bam,pb,male,y

lrsomatic extracts information from the bam header files to decide which models to use for Clair3, ClairS, or ClairS-TO. However, this can optionally be specified manually. You can do this for one or many samples, if the field is left blank, the pipeline will default to extracting this information. You can specify this by creating your csv in the following form:

sample,bam_tumor,bam_normal,platform,sex,fiber,clair3_model,clairSTO_model,clairS_model
sample1,tumour.bam,normal.bam,ont,female,n
sample2,tumour.bam,,ont,female,y
sample3,tumour.bam,normal.bam,pb,male,n,r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v420,,ont_r10_dorado_sup_5khz_ssrs
sample4,tumour.bam,normal.bam,pb,male,y

The aligned BAM/CRAM files lrsomatic publishes do not carry the basecaller model (their @RG lines keep ID, SM, LB and PL only), so to feed them back in as ONT input, fill in clair3_model, clairSTO_model and clairS_model for those rows.

Use the input parameter to specify the location to this input csv.

--input '[path to samplesheet file]'

docs.title: Multiple runs of the same sample
docs.text:
The sample identifiers have to be the same when you have re-sequenced the same sample more than once e.g. to increase sequencing depth. Each file is aligned on its own, then the alignments of a sample are merged per type (tumour, normal) with SAMTOOLS_MERGE before any downstream analysis. The tumor_replicate and normal_replicate columns number the rows of a sample (1, 2, ...); they name each file's alignment and its read group (@RG ID:<sample>_<type>_rep<N>), so the replicates stay distinguishable in the merged file. Keep platform, sex, fiber and the model columns the same on every row of a sample.

A tumour-only sample sequenced three times:

sample,bam_tumor,bam_normal,platform,sex,fiber,clair3_model,clairSTO_model,clairS_model,tumor_replicate,normal_replicate
sample1,tumour1.bam,,ont,female,n,,,,1,
sample1,tumour2.bam,,ont,female,n,,,,2,
sample1,tumour3.bam,,ont,female,n,,,,3,

For a matched sample, every row needs its own tumour file and its own normal file, with distinct replicate numbers:

sample,bam_tumor,bam_normal,platform,sex,fiber,clair3_model,clairSTO_model,clairS_model,tumor_replicate,normal_replicate
sample2,tumour1.bam,normal1.bam,pb,male,n,,,,1,1
sample2,tumour2.bam,normal2.bam,pb,male,n,,,,2,2

This gives one merged tumour, one merged normal and one paired analysis. The pipeline stops at start-up, naming the sample, for encodings that this merge would otherwise mis-handle:

  • some rows of a sample have a bam_normal and others do not (the tumour rows would not be merged with each other, and the sample could not be paired correctly);
  • the same normal file is listed on more than one row (it would be merged with itself), or one file is listed as both bam_tumor and bam_normal;
  • two rows of a sample share a tumor_replicate, or two rows with a normal share a normal_replicate. A blank replicate counts as 1, so a sample with several rows needs both columns filled in;
  • rows of a sample differ in platform, sex or fiber.

The model columns are checked later, once each file's basecaller model has been read from its header (after METAEXTRACT): the run stops if a sample's files resolve to different clair3_model, clairSTO_model or clairS_model values, whether set in the samplesheet or detected from the headers.

The same tumour file on more than one row only gives a warning, since it is merged with itself as well. To use one normal with several tumour files, merge the tumour files into one BAM beforehand (samtools merge) and give the sample a single row, or split the normal into one file per row.

docs.title: Full Description of Samplesheet Columns
docs.text:
Column Description sample Custom sample name. This entry will be identical for multiple sequencing libraries/runs from the same sample. Spaces in sample names are automatically converted to underscores (_). bam_tumor Full path to the BAM or CRAM file of the tumour. File must end in .bam or .cram (see CRAM input). bam_normal Full path to the BAM or CRAM file of the normal (optional). File must end in .bam or .cram. platform A string specifying the platform used for sequencing, can be either pb for PacBio sequencing data or ont for Oxford Nanopore sequencing data sex A string specifying the biological sex of the sample, can either be male or female fiber A string specifying if the sample has been subjected to Fiber-seq. Can either be y or n; a y row whose reads carry no m6A calls skips the fiber steps (see Fiber-seq rows without m6A calls) clair3_model A Clair3 model name (optional). Clair3 v2 only reads PyTorch models: names bundled with Clair3 (e.g. r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v500, hifi_revio) are used from the image, other ONT names are downloaded from HKU's PyTorch conversion of Rerio clairSTO_model A string describing which model is to be used for ClairS-TO's small variant calling (optional) clairS_model A string describing which model is to be used for ClairS's small variant calling (optional) tumor_replicate Integer numbering the rows of a sample with several tumour files (optional, blank = 1); see Multiple runs of the same sample normal_replicate Integer numbering the rows of a sample with several normal files (optional, blank = 1)

An example samplesheet has been provided with the pipeline.

docs.title: CRAM input
docs.text:
The input reads may be BAM or CRAM, and BAM and CRAM can be mixed in one samplesheet. Every input is realigned (unless --skip_alignment is set), so it can be unaligned or aligned to any assembly. An unaligned CRAM (e.g. samtools reset -O cram) needs no reference. An aligned CRAM can only be read with the reference it was written against:

  • a CRAM with the reference embedded (--output-fmt-option embed_ref=1, as lrsomatic writes) always works;
  • a CRAM aligned to the same assembly as --fasta works: the pipeline decodes it with --fasta, after checking that no contig name has a different checksum (M5) in the two;
  • a CRAM aligned to another assembly is decoded from its embedded reference, the UR: path in its header or htslib's REF_PATH/REF_CACHE (with REF_PATH unset, htslib downloads the sequence from the EBI reference server), never from --fasta. If none of those is reachable from the tasks, the run stops with an htslib Unable to fetch reference error.

In practice the UR: path is often enough: it works whenever that path is visible inside the containers (e.g. a filesystem your profile binds). Some tools (e.g. cramino in CRAMINO_PRE) first try the EBI reference server and log a failed request before falling back to UR:; where the server is reachable, they download the contigs from it. A CRAM whose reference differs from --fasta in any contig checksum (e.g. a masked chrY or another chrM) is not decoded with --fasta, even when the assembly name is the same. A CRAM aligned to the GATK GRCh38 FASTA passes that check against the default GRCh38 reference and is decoded with it, but its reads on ALT, HLA and decoy contigs, which the default lacks, still need the embedded reference, UR: or REF_PATH.

Fiber-seq samples (fiber = y, unless they carry no m6A calls) and PacBio data with kinetics are read by fibertools-rs before alignment, and fibertools-rs cannot take a reference. Aligned input for these samples, BAM or CRAM, therefore first goes through SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP, which writes the primary records as BAM: secondary and supplementary records are dropped (samtools view -F 0x900), since fibertools-rs crashes on the secondary alignments minimap2 writes by default and the pipeline's realignment drops both anyway. An aligned CRAM is decoded there by the rules above, so it works if it embeds its reference or matches --fasta. Otherwise SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP fails for that sample with htslib's Failed to populate reference error, unless its UR: path or REF_PATH is reachable: write the CRAM with --output-fmt-option embed_ref=1, convert it to BAM, or run with the --fasta it was aligned to.

docs.title: Aligned input
docs.text:
Aligned input (BAM or CRAM with @SQ lines) is turned back into reads before alignment: MINIMAP2_ALIGN runs samtools reset | samtools fastq -T '*' and minimap2 -y, which copies every read tag into the new records. For aligned input the reset step drops the tags that describe the old alignment or its phasing, so none is duplicated or carried over stale into the new alignment:

  • everything samtools reset drops by default (AS, CC, CG, CP, H0, H1, H2, HI, IH, MC, MD, MQ, NM, SA, TS);
  • minimap2's tags tp, cm, s1, s2, nn, ms, de, dv, rl, zd, cs, cg, ds, which minimap2 writes again for the new alignment (dropped from unaligned input too, see below);
  • phasing tags HP, PS, PQ, PC (from WhatsHap, LongPhase or HiPhase, including the pipeline's own haplotagged output), which would otherwise give Severus, SAVANA, Wakhan and modkit the phasing of the old alignment;
  • OA, XA, XS (original alignment, other aligners' alternative hits), and the read group RG, which is replaced by the pipeline's own.

Every other tag is kept, in particular base modifications (MM, ML, MN), fibertools-rs output and read-level tags written by Dorado or the PacBio instruments (qs, ns, ts, mv, pi, sp, np, rq, sn, ec, zm, ...). The one exception is the PacBio kinetics (fi, fp, ri, rp, ip, pw): they are dropped from every PacBio row, aligned or not, unless --keep_kinetic_data is set (see PacBio kinetics). This is a deny-list rather than an allow-list on purpose: the read-level tags vary with the basecaller version and chemistry, and an allow-list would silently drop one a user or a downstream tool relies on. The cost is that a tag from an aligner or phasing tool not listed above survives the realignment; if your input carries such tags, remove them first (e.g. samtools view -x). Dorado's ts:i (trimmed samples) has the same name as minimap2's ts:A (transcript strand, splice mode only) and is kept. For aligned and unaligned input alike, float tags (type f, e.g. Dorado's qs, du, sd) pass through FASTQ header text, which samtools writes with 6 significant digits and has no option to widen, so their binary values can differ from the input in the last digits (qs:f:22.1447 prints the same before and after).

Unaligned input keeps every tag except RG, minimap2's tags above and, for PacBio, the kinetics (unless --keep_kinetic_data is set). An unaligned BAM can still carry minimap2's tags: Dorado writes them when it aligns, and a uBAM made from such a file may keep some (e.g. zd, minimap2's z-drop split flag, which Dorado itself treats as an alignment tag); minimap2 -y would then write them twice.

Each samplesheet row gets one new read group, @RG ID:<sample>_<type>_rep<replicate>. For ONT input whose header names its basecalling model (Dorado's DS:basecall_model=...), the model is written into that read group as DS:basecall_model=<model>, so a BAM/CRAM published by the pipeline can be fed back in without filling the model columns of the samplesheet. A merged file fed back in as one row also gets one read group: the per-replicate read groups of the earlier run (..._rep1, ..._rep2, ...) are collapsed into one, so give the replicates as separate rows (from the original input files) if you need them kept apart.

docs.title: Skipping alignment
docs.text:
--skip_alignment uses the input files as the alignment instead of realigning them with minimap2, which saves the most expensive step of the run. It is meant for files that were already aligned to the pipeline reference. We still recommend realigning: the variant-calling models assume minimap2 alignments made with the pipeline's settings, and other aligners or presets can change the calls.

Every input file must meet all of these conditions, or the run stops:

  • it is aligned (has @SQ lines);
  • every @SQ contig is in --fasta with the same length. The check uses names and lengths only, so a masked or otherwise edited copy of the same assembly passes;
  • it is coordinate-sorted (SO:coordinate in the @HD line);
  • it is not read by fibertools-rs, which runs before alignment. This excludes fiber = y rows and PacBio rows with kinetics while m6A is predicted. Use --skip_fiber or --skip_m6a to run those rows without the Fiber-seq or m6A steps, or run without --skip_alignment.

The files are not used as they are. PREPARE_ALIGNED makes one samtools pass over each file that:

  • replaces its read groups with the pipeline's own (@RG ID:<sample>_<type>_rep<replicate>, with DS:basecall_model= for ONT input whose header names the model, as after alignment);
  • drops the phasing tags HP, PS, PQ and PC, and for PacBio the kinetics unless --keep_kinetic_data is set, as the realignment does (see Aligned input);
  • writes --aligned_format (CRAM 3.0 with the reference embedded, by default) and indexes it.

An aligned CRAM input is decoded as described in CRAM input. All other records and tags are kept as they are, including hard-clipped supplementary alignments and the aligner's own tags. Secondary alignments are kept unless --save_secondary_alignment false is set, as after alignment. Replicates of a sample are merged as usual. CRAMINO_PRE and NANOPLOT_PRE do not run, since the input is the alignment that CRAMINO_POST reports on.

docs.title: PacBio kinetics
docs.text: PacBio HiFi reads written with --keep-kinetics carry per-base kinetics (fi, fp, ri, rp), which fibertools-rs uses to call m6A and which make up a large share of a BAM. By default the pipeline drops them (and the per-subread ip/pw, if present) from every PacBio read when the reads are converted for alignment, so no aligned or published file carries them: not the reads ft predict-m6a gave no m6A call (it strips the kinetics only from the reads it calls, leaving them on about 2-3 % of reads), and not the samples that never reach it (--skip_m6a, --skip_fiber, or normals under --skip_normalfiber). Base modifications (MM/ML), fibertools-rs tags and the other PacBio read tags, including the kinetics pass counts fn/rn, are kept. With --keep_kinetic_data true the kinetics are kept on every read instead (ft predict-m6a --keep, and nothing dropped at alignment).

docs.title: Fiber-seq rows without m6A calls
docs.text:
Nucleosome and FIRE calling (FIBERTOOLSRS_NUCLEOSOMES, FIBERTOOLSRS_FIRE) and the fibertools-rs QC work from the m6A calls in the reads. METAEXTRACT looks for an m6A entry (A+a, T-a or ChEBI 28871) in the MM tags of the first 1000 records of each input file. A fiber-seq file (fiber = y) without one, for which the run predicts no m6A either, skips these steps (and SAMTOOLS_VIEW_FIBERPREP) with a warning naming the sample and the reason, and goes on to alignment like a fiber = n row: on such reads the steps report zero m6A, nucleosomes and MSPs and write a full copy of the input. The pipeline predicts m6A (FIBERTOOLSRS_PREDICTM6A) only for PacBio reads with kinetics (written with --keep-kinetics) when --skip_m6a is not set, so this applies to:

  • ONT reads, which carry m6A calls only when basecalled with a 6mA modified-base model;
  • PacBio reads without kinetics;
  • PacBio reads with kinetics under --skip_m6a.

PacBio reads with kinetics without --skip_m6a get m6A predicted and then go through the fiber steps. A file whose first records could not be read keeps the fiber steps. A skipped file has no fibertoolsrs/ QC file in the output.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
The typical command for running the pipeline is as follows:

nextflow run IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic --input ./samplesheet.csv --outdir ./results --genome GRCh38 -profile docker

This will launch the pipeline with the docker configuration profile. See below for more information about profiles.

Note that the pipeline will create the following files in your working directory:

work                # Directory containing the nextflow working files
<OUTDIR>            # Finished results in specified location (defined with --outdir)
.nextflow_log       # Log file from Nextflow
# Other nextflow hidden files, eg. history of pipeline runs and old logs.

[!WARNING] Do not use -c <file> to specify parameters as this will result in errors. Custom config files specified with -c must only be used for tuning process resource specifications, other infrastructural tweaks (such as output directories), or module arguments (args).

The above pipeline run specified with a params file in yaml format:

nextflow run IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic -profile docker -params-file params.yaml

with:

params.yaml
input: './samplesheet.csv'
outdir: './results/'
genome: 'GRCh37'
<...>

You can also generate such YAML/JSON files via nf-core/launch.

docs.title: GRCh38 reference
docs.text:
--genome GRCh38 aligns to the NCBI no-ALT analysis set, GCA_000001405.15_GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set, staged from the iGenomes copy at ${igenomes_base}/Homo_sapiens/NCBI/GRCh38/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/genome.fa (byte-identical to NCBI's .fna.gz once decompressed). It has 195 chr-named contigs: chr1-22, chrX, chrY, chrM, 127 unlocalized and unplaced contigs (*_random, chrUn_*) and chrEBV, with no ALT, HLA or decoy contigs. The chrY PARs and the duplicated centromeric arrays are hard-masked, as in other analysis sets.

Up to lrsomatic 1.1.0 the default was the GATK Homo_sapiens_assembly38.fasta, which adds 261 ALT, 525 HLA and 2,385 decoy contigs. minimap2 is not ALT-aware, so reads from regions with an ALT haplotype were split between the primary contig and the ALT contig, mostly at mapping quality 0, and variant calling in those regions (the MHC most of all) lost most of its calls. Every contig of the no-ALT set is in the GATK FASTA under the same name, length and M5, so all other GRCh38 resources (ASCAT, panels of normals, VEP, SigProfiler, Padfoot, SAVANA, Wakhan) apply unchanged. Results differ from earlier runs in ALT regions, and -resume from an earlier version realigns every sample. To keep the previous reference, pass --fasta s3://ngi-igenomes/igenomes/Homo_sapiens/GATK/GRCh38/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/Homo_sapiens_assembly38.fasta.

docs.title: CHM13 Support
docs.text:
Our pipeline fully supports CHM13 and most reference and annotation files are automatically downloaded when specifying --genome CHM13.

However, VEP will need a bit of additional setup. The VEP cache for CHM13 needs to be manually downloaded. This can be done using the following code. Feel free to change any of the paths, ensuring that the correct path is pointed to in the pipeline parameters.

Download CHM13 Cache:

cd $HOME/.vep
curl -O https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/rapid-release/species/Homo_sapiens/GCA_009914755.4/ensembl/variation/2022_10/indexed_vep_cache/Homo_sapiens-GCA_009914755.4-2022_10.tar.gz
tar xzf Homo_sapiens-GCA_009914755.4-2022_10.tar.gz

Then you can run the pipeline as follows:

nextflow run IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir ./results \
  --genome CHM13 \
  --vep_cache $HOME/.vep \
  --vep_cache_version 107 \
  -profile docker

If you want to run with a CHM13 reference without using --genome CHM13 (for example, via a custom FASTA or configuration), you must also specify --vep_genome T2T-CHM13v2.0 and --vep_species homo_sapiens_gca009914755v4.

This cache carries gene and transcript models only, so every pathogenicity score on CHM13 has to come from a plugin. With --genome CHM13 the pipeline fetches those itself; note that only the two predictors keyed on protein rather than genome coordinates can reach the assembly at all. See VEP plugins for which those are and why. The cache has no known-variant or population-frequency data either, so on CHM13 the Existing_variation, AF, gnomAD* and CLIN_SIG CSQ fields are empty for every variant, --filter_common in --vep_args removes nothing, and ClinVar annotation comes only from the pipeline's CHM13-lifted ClinVar --custom VCF.

Setting --vep_genome T2T-CHM13v2.0 by hand, without --genome CHM13, resolves no plugin defaults — supply the --vep_* paths yourself, or accept VEP without plugin annotation.

For mutational signatures, --genome CHM13 selects the CHM13-T2T SigProfilerMatrixGenerator genome. Its payload is not on the AlexandrovLab FTP yet, so the default download fetches it from the IntGenomicsLab Globus collection (--sigprofiler_genome_url); see Mutational Signature Options.

For structural variants, the CHM13 panel of normals is a merged panel combining the 1000 Genomes CHM13 panel shipped with SEVERUS and the ASAP cohort, with median confidence intervals per breakpoint. The pipeline exposes it as --pon_file and hands it to SEVERUS via that tool's own --PON flag; it is downloaded automatically with --genome CHM13. GRCh38 continues to use the 1000 Genomes panel shipped with SEVERUS.

For tumour-only small variants, ClairS-TO separates germline from somatic calls with a panel of normals and with its Verdict module, which tags each call as germline, somatic or subclonal somatic from tumour purity and allele-specific copy number. --genome CHM13 supplies five CHM13 PON VCFs (gnomAD, dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, CoLoRSdb and ASAP), which replace the GRCh38 databases inside the container. Unless --skip_ascat is set, purity and copy number come from the pipeline's own ASCAT run (CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG); only with --skip_ascat does ClairS-TO estimate them itself, from assembly-specific loci, allele and GC content files. A GRCh38 resource set on a CHM13 run leaves germline variants untagged.

Verdict only tags when the tumour purity is at most 0.6: the cut-off is ClairS-TO's own (src/verdict/tag_germline_variant.py), and it applies on every assembly, whether the purity comes from ASCAT (CLAIRSTO_VERDICT_TAG) or, with --skip_ascat, from Verdict itself. Above it the calls are passed through untagged; the only trace is a [WARNING] Tumor purity estimation ... is higher than 0.6 line in the task's .command.out, not in the pipeline log or the report. Germline variants then only leave the somatic set through the panel of normals, and in practice most of them stay: in tumour-only runs on real samples with purities of 0.66-0.82, 73-93 % of the PASS "somatic" SNVs had a VAF of 0.35 or more, i.e. were mostly germline. Check {sample}_Tumor_Purity_Ploidy.txt under variants/clairsto/ before using tumour-only somatic calls of a high-purity tumour, and treat high-VAF calls with care.

When --germline_var_keep includes deepvariant, the tumour-only germline arm runs DeepVariant on the tumour BAM, so on its own those calls mix germline and clonal somatic variants. When deepsomatic is also in --somatic_var_keep, the pipeline keeps a DeepVariant PASS record only when every allele its genotype carries matches (CHROM, POS, REF, ALT, after splitting and left-aligning both callers' records) a DeepSomatic record whose FILTER includes GERMLINE or PON, whatever --smallvar_filter_pass is. The record is published as DeepVariant wrote it, with its own genotype and all its ALT alleles. A DeepVariant record is dropped when any of its called alleles is one DeepSomatic calls PASS (somatic) or RefCall, or never evaluated: e.g. DeepVariant C>CCG,CG 1/2 of which only CCG has a GERMLINE verdict is left out rather than published as C>CCG 1/0, and DeepVariant G>GTT,GTTT 2/2 whose verdict covers only the uncalled GTT is left out rather than published as G>GTT 0/0 (as earlier versions did). Without deepsomatic, DeepVariant's PASS germline calls are used without a verdict filter and may include somatic variants. Either way the tumour-only germline arm is a tumour-derived proxy, not a call set from normal tissue.

With --genome CHM13 --skip_ascat the pipeline builds a CHM13 resource set from the ASCAT files it already downloads, so no extra setup is needed. LogR correction is GC-only, as ClairS-TO recommends for CHM13: no replication timing file is published for the assembly. Without --skip_ascat nothing is built, because the tagging comes from ASCAT's own tables.

To use a resource set of your own — another assembly, or a CHM13 set carrying an RT_<name>.txt for replication timing correction — pass --clairsto_cna_resources together with --skip_ascat. Without --skip_ascat it is ignored, with a warning. Expected layout:

<dir>/
  loci_files/<prefix>chr1.txt ... <prefix>chr22.txt, <prefix>chrX.txt
  allele_files/<prefix>chr1.txt ... <prefix>chr22.txt, <prefix>chrX.txt
  GC_<name>.txt
  RT_<name>.txt        (optional; without it, correction is GC-only)

Keep one resource set per directory: ClairS-TO derives the per-contig prefix from the single *chr1.txt and takes exactly one GC_*.txt. The directory must be self-contained, since only the directory itself is staged into the container; materialise symlinked content with cp -rL. Both are checked at startup.

If the loci cannot belong to the reference, ClairS-TO disables Verdict with a warning rather than applying the wrong coordinates. On a --skip_ascat run, look for VERDICT CNA RESOURCE DIRECTORY in the ClairS-TO log to confirm which set was used; otherwise Verdict runs outside ClairS-TO and the tables the tags came from are published next to the VCFs.

Padfoot bundles gene and repeat annotations for hg38 and mm10 only. With --genome CHM13 it is skipped with a warning unless you also pass --padfoot_gff and --padfoot_rm (see Padfoot Options). Padfoot reads each 51-bp reference window around a breakpoint as one FASTA line, so for a FASTA wrapped at fewer than 51 columns (the iGenomes CHM13 genome.fa is wrapped at 50) the module writes a re-wrapped copy for Padfoot only; this takes about a minute and 3 GB of temporary space per task and is deleted when the task ends. ReConPlot (T2T preset) and ShatterSeek (chm13) need nothing extra on CHM13.

docs.title: Pipeline options
docs.text:
Parameter Description -input Full file path to input samplesheet, must be in .csv format and conform to specifications noted above --genome Specified genome assembly, support is given for GRCh38 and CHM13

To skip fiber-seq processing of the normal files of a pair whose tumour has fiber-seq, use --skip_normalfiber (see Skipping options).

docs.title: Skipping options:
docs.text: Parameter Description --skip_qc A boolean to skip all QC steps, including mosdepth, samtools,fibertools, cramino. Default = false --skip_fiber A boolean to skip all fibertools related modules. Default = false --skip_cramino A boolean to skip cramino. Default = false --skip_mosdepth A boolean to skip mosdepth. Default = false --skip_ascat A boolean to skip ascat. ClairS-TO's Verdict germline tagging then falls back to Verdict's own purity and copy number estimate, which is still up to 0.14 from ASCAT's on the samples it was measured on — see Verdict tags. Default = false --skip_savana A boolean to skip savana (SV + copy-number calling). Default = false --skip_padfoot A boolean to skip padfoot SV/CNA annotation. Default = false --skip_reconplot A boolean to skip reconplot SV/CNA figures. Default = false --skip_shatterseek A boolean to skip shatterseek chromothripsis calling. Default = false --skip_bamstats A boolean to skip bamstats. Default = false --skip_wakhan A boolean to skip wakhan. Default = false --skip_vep A boolean to skip vep. Default = false --skip_m6a A boolean to skip fibertools_m6a for PacBio data with kinetics, e.g. when the reads already carry m6A calls (ONT reads only have their basecaller's m6A calls). With it, a PacBio file with kinetics but no m6A calls also skips the nucleosome, FIRE and fibertools-rs QC steps; ONT files and PacBio files without kinetics that carry no m6A calls skip them either way (see Fiber-seq rows without m6A calls). Default = false --skip_nanoplot A boolean to skip NanoPlot QC on aligned and unaligned BAM files. Default = false --skip_normalfiber A boolean to skip fibertools processing for the normal sample. Default = false --skip_modcall A boolean to skip Longphase modcall, the 5mC base-modification calling whose VCF is used as extra evidence during phasing. Unrelated to the modkit pileup (see --skip_modkit). Default = false --skip_modkit A boolean to skip the modkit pileup step. Default = false --skip_dmr A boolean to skip haplotype differential methylation region (DMR) calling. Only takes effect when --modkit_phased is also set; has no effect otherwise. Default = false --skip_whatshapstats A boolean to skip WhatsHap phasing statistics. Default = false --skip_signatures A boolean to skip mutational signature analysis (SigProfilerMatrixGenerator + SigProfilerAssignment). Default = false --skip_report A boolean to skip the final per-sample HTML report. Default = false --skip_report_hmf A boolean to skip the report's HMF driver annotation, which is on by default for GRCh38 and CHM13 (see HMF driver annotation). Default = false

docs.title: Modkit options:
docs.text:
Parameter Description --modkit_args Arguments passed to modkit pileup. The value replaces the default rather than extending it, so repeat --cpg --modified-bases 5mC when adding flags. An empty value gives the unfiltered pileup: use the = form, --modkit_args='', or an empty modkit_args entry in a params file. Default = --cpg --modified-bases 5mC --modkit_phased Run modkit pileup --phased on the Longphase-haplotagged BAMs, producing _hp1, _hp2 and _combined bedMethyl files per sample. The pileup then requires small-variant calling, phasing and haplotagging to have succeeded for the sample. Default = false

The pileup runs a patched modkit 0.6.4 image (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/modkit, linux/amd64 only, built from ljwharbers/modkit@pacbio-conflict-fix): stock modkit drops PacBio HiFi reads whose 5mC and 5hmC probabilities sum above 1 and returns empty --cpg pileups on them (nanoporetech/modkit#612). Conda and arm64 are not supported for this step; use --skip_modkit there.

docs.title: DMR options:
docs.text:
With --modkit_phased set, haplotype differential methylation region (DMR) calling runs automatically unless --skip_dmr is given: modkit dmr pair compares methylation between the _hp1/_hp2 bedMethyl pileups over CpG islands covered in both haplotypes, and the result is annotated with its nearest gene.

Parameter Description --skip_dmr Skip DMR calling. Only takes effect when --modkit_phased is also set. Default = false --dmr_cpg_islands_bed CpG-islands BED to restrict DMR calling to. Has a built-in default for --genome GRCh38/CHM13; required as an explicit override for any other genome. Default = null (built-in default for GRCh38/CHM13) --dmr_gencode_gene_bed Gene-model BED used to annotate each DMR call with its nearest gene. Has a built-in default for --genome GRCh38/CHM13; required as an explicit override for any other genome. Default = null (built-in default for GRCh38/CHM13)

On any other genome, DMR is skipped with a log.warn (not a hard failure) unless both BEDs are supplied explicitly. --modkit_args's default only requests 5mC calls, but ONT SUP-basecalled data also calls 5hmC at the same sites, and modkit dmr pair rejects bedMethyl rows whose valid coverage includes calls of an unrequested modification code. So whenever DMR will run (--modkit_phased set, --skip_dmr not set, both BEDs available), 5hmC is appended to --modified-bases if it names 5mC without it. DMR reads the same pileup that is published, so the published modkit_pileup/*_{hp1,hp2,combined}.bed.gz then contain a 5hmC row next to each 5mC row. Use --skip_dmr to keep --modkit_args exactly as given.

docs.title: LONGPHASE options:
docs.text: Parameter Description --longphase_tag_supplementary Include supplementary alignments in Longphase haplotype tagging. Default = false

docs.title: VEP options:
docs.text: Parameter Description --vep_cache Full path to a vep cache. If left blank, this will default to pulling from this Annotation Cache Storage. --vep_cache_version Integer specifying version of vep cache. Default = 113 --vep_args A string specifying arguments to vep. Default = "--everything --filter_common --per_gene --total_length --offline --format vcf --vcf" --vep_custom A full path to a vcf file containing custom variants for annotation. Must be bgzipped and have .vcf.gz format. Default = null --vep_custom_tbi A full path to a index file for cutom vcf for vep. Default = null --download_vep_cache A boolean to automatically download the VEP cache if not found locally. Default = false --outdir_cache Directory the downloaded VEP cache (--download_vep_cache) and SigProfiler genome payload (sigprofiler/volume) are published to. Default = <outdir>/cache

docs.title: VEP plugin options:
docs.text:
The plugin data is on by default on --genome GRCh38 and --genome CHM13; setting a parameter overrides its default, --skip_vep_plugins turns the set off, and CADD and EVE are opt-in. See VEP plugins for sizes, licence terms and per-assembly availability.

Parameter Description --skip_vep_plugins Annotate with VEP alone, fetching no plugin data. Default = false --vep_alphamissense AlphaMissense GRCh38 score file, for the AlphaMissense plugin. GRCh38 only --vep_alphamissense_tbi Index for --vep_alphamissense. Required whenever --vep_alphamissense is set --vep_alphamissense_aa Prepared gene-symbol-keyed table for the AlphaMissenseProtein plugin (see below). CHM13 only --vep_alphamissense_aa_tbi Index for --vep_alphamissense_aa. Required whenever --vep_alphamissense_aa is set --vep_polyphen_sift_db Ensembl pangenome PolyPhen/SIFT SQLite database, for the PolyPhen_SIFT plugin. Needed on CHM13 only --vep_clinvar ClinVar VCF, added as a VEP --custom annotation --vep_clinvar_tbi Index for --vep_clinvar. Required whenever --vep_clinvar is set --vep_clinvar_md5 Expected MD5 of a remote --vep_clinvar, checked after download. Dropped when --vep_clinvar is overridden --vep_clinvar_tbi_md5 Expected MD5 of the downloaded --vep_clinvar_tbi. Set on CHM13 only; dropped when either ClinVar file is overridden --vep_clinvar_fields Comma-separated ClinVar INFO fields to carry through. Default = "CLNSIG,CLNREVSTAT,CLNDN" --vep_cadd_snv CADD SNV score file, for the CADD plugin. No default — 81 GB, so opt-in; prefer a local path. GRCh38 only --vep_cadd_snv_tbi Index for --vep_cadd_snv. Required whenever --vep_cadd_snv is set --vep_cadd_indel CADD indel score file, for the CADD plugin. No default — opt-in. GRCh38 only --vep_cadd_indel_tbi Index for --vep_cadd_indel. Required whenever --vep_cadd_indel is set --vep_revel REVEL release zip, or a prepared score file, for the REVEL plugin. GRCh38 only --vep_revel_tbi Index for --vep_revel. Required only when --vep_revel is an already-prepared file --vep_eve EVE release zip, or a merged VCF, for the EVE plugin. Not on by default. GRCh38 only. Default = null --vep_eve_tbi Index for --vep_eve. Required only when --vep_eve is an already-merged VCF. Default = null

--vep_alphamissense_aa is used as given: unlike REVEL and EVE, the pipeline does not build it from the AlphaMissense release. The CHM13 default is a table we host. A replacement must be a bgzipped, tab-separated file whose first line is a #-prefixed header with at least gene (gene symbol), aapos (1-based residue), aaref and aaalt (one-letter amino acids), plus the score columns to report (by default am_pathogenicity and am_class; the hosted table also has uniprot_acc), sorted by gene and position and indexed with tabix -s 1 -b 2 -e 2 -c "#". The hosted table is AlphaMissense's AlphaMissense_aa_substitutions.tsv.gz with the UniProt accession mapped to a gene symbol and the protein variant (e.g. V2L) split into those three columns; see CITATIONS.md.

docs.title: Minimap2 Options
docs.text:
Parameter Description --minimap2_ont_model specifies which model to use minimap2 with for ONT samples. Default = null --minimap2_pb_model specifies which model to use minimap2 with for PacBio samples. Default = null --save_secondary_alignment A boolean to specify if secondary alignments are kept in aligned bam file. Default = true --aligned_format cram or bam: format of the aligned and haplotagged reads. Default = cram (see below) --skip_alignment Use the input alignments instead of realigning them; see Skipping alignment. Default = false

--aligned_format cram writes CRAM 3.0 with the reference embedded, from alignment onwards and in bamfiles/. On long reads this is a third (ONT) to two thirds (PacBio Revio) smaller than BAM, with identical records and the same calls from every tool in the pipeline. Because the reference is embedded, the files can be read without the FASTA. Use --aligned_format bam if a tool you run on the results cannot read CRAM, or convert afterwards with samtools view -b -o sample_tumor.bam sample_tumor.cram.

docs.title: ASCAT Options
docs.text: Parameter Description --ascat_ploidy integer to enforce a given ploidy value. Default = null --ascat_purity integer to enforce a given purity value. Default = null --ascat_min_base_qual integer to specify a minimum base quality for ascat's allele counter. Default = 20 --ascat_min_counts integer to specify a minimum number of counts for ascat's allele counter. Default = 10 --ascat_min_map_qual integer to specify a minimum mapping quality for ascat's allele counter. Default = 10 --ascat_penalty integer to specify a penalty value for ascat. Default = 150 --ascat_longread_bins integer to specify the binsize for ascat long reads. Default = 2000 --ascat_allelecounter_flags flags to pass to ascat's allele counter. Default = "-f 0" --ascat_chroms string to enforce a subset of chromosomes on the sample, ie "(c(1:21,'X','Y')). Default =null` --ascat_allele_files Allele files for ASCAT: a .zip containing one folder, or the path to that folder, whose files are named <folder>_chr<N>.txt. Default = the --genome reference (GRCh38, CHM13) --ascat_loci_files Loci files for ASCAT: a .zip containing one folder, or the path to that folder, whose files are named <folder>_chr<N>.txt. Default = the --genome reference (GRCh38, CHM13) --ascat_gc_file GC correction file for ASCAT, as .txt or .txt.zip. Default = the --genome reference (GRCh38, CHM13) --ascat_rt_file Replication timing correction file for ASCAT, as .txt or .txt.zip. Default = the --genome reference (GRCh38 only; CHM13 has none, so ASCAT corrects for GC only) --ascat_pdf_plots string to enable output pltos in pdf format. Default = false

docs.title: Fibertools Options
docs.text: Parameter Description --autocorrelation A boolean to enable autocorrelation computation in fibertools. Default = false --keep_kinetic_data A boolean to keep the PacBio kinetics tags (fi, fp, ri, rp) on every read. It passes --keep to ft predict-m6a, which otherwise strips them from the reads it calls m6A on, and it also turns off the removal of kinetics from PacBio reads at alignment. By default they are removed, which keeps the aligned files much smaller. Default = false --keep_all_calls A boolean to keep every m6A call regardless of its ML score (ft predict-m6a --all-calls). Default = false

docs.title: SEVERUS Options
docs.text:
Parameter Description --severus_minsupport Minimum number of supporting reads required for SEVERUS to call an SV. Default = 3 --severus_whitelist BED file of regions in which SVs are reported past Severus' filters (Severus --whitelist; see below). Its VCFs feed SV VEP, Wakhan, Padfoot, ReConPlot, ShatterSeek and the report as usual. Default = off --severus_whitelist_args Extra arguments for SEVERUS, only used with --severus_whitelist: the --whitelist-* options below, or e.g. --write-alignments. Appended after --min-support <severus_minsupport> --output-read-ids. Default = none

SEVERUS runs a patched Severus 1.7 build (AmberVerhasselt/Severus) from oras://docker.io/amberverhasselt/severus-sif (docker.io/amberverhasselt/severus under Docker); without --severus_whitelist its output is identical to stock Severus 1.7. Inside the whitelisted regions it skips the read-quality (mapping quality, mismatch rate, aligned length), minimum-support and VNTR filters. Every SV within a whitelisted region carries INFO/INSIDE_WHITELIST=TRUE, and one that was kept only because of the whitelist carries INFO/WL_RESCUE with the reason: WHITELIST (inside a region), RECIPROCAL (a reciprocal junction corroborates it) or SUPPORTED_NEIGHBOUR (a neighbouring junction with independent read support does). This is meant for loci such as the IG and TCR genes, where translocations are often carried by few, divergent reads. --severus_whitelist is not supported under Conda, which installs stock Severus.

The whitelist build adds these options, passed through --severus_whitelist_args (e.g. --severus_whitelist_args '--whitelist-reciprocal-dist 2000 --whitelist-enforce-mapq'):

Severus option Effect --whitelist-single-read reciprocal\|any\|off What to do with a whitelisted junction supported by a single read: keep it only when a reciprocal or independently supported junction corroborates it (reciprocal), keep it unconditionally (any) or drop it (off). Default = reciprocal --whitelist-reciprocal-dist <int> Maximum distance (bp) at both breakends to a corroborating junction for reciprocal. Default = 1000 --whitelist-allow-intra-region Also rescue single-read junctions with both breakends in the same whitelisted region. Physiological V(D)J recombination inside an IG/TCR locus is then reported as somatic. Default = off --whitelist-enforce-mapq Apply Severus' --min-mapq (default 10) inside whitelisted regions too, so the whitelist exempts only the mismatch-rate and aligned-length checks. Default = off

[!WARNING] --whitelist-single-read any floods 30x whole-genome data with single-read artefacts. On a 30x ONT pair with a non-Hodgkin lymphoma gene whitelist it gave 9,711 somatic SVs, 9,388 of them rescued, against 314 without a whitelist; the default reciprocal rescued 47-444 SVs per sample on the same kind of data. Rescued SVs are not filtered out downstream: they reach SV VEP, Padfoot, ShatterSeek (where they can produce chromothripsis calls) and ReConPlot. Use any only on small targeted regions, and check INFO/WL_RESCUE when reading the results.

docs.title: SAVANA Options
docs.text:
SAVANA reuses the haplotagged BAMs from PHASING_HAPLOTYPING and the same reference FASTA/index as every other caller. Matched tumor/normal samples run savana run + savana classify + savana cna, using the phased germline VCF as the SNP allele-frequency source for copy-number fitting; tumor-only samples run savana to instead (which chains the equivalent steps internally), using SAVANA's bundled 1000 Genomes population SNP set rather than the tumour's own calls. SV calling (savana run, savana to) is restricted to canonical chromosomes via a genome-specific --contigs file. Copy-number calling needs no such file: SAVANA 1.3.8 only ever bins and counts alleles on chr1-22, chrX and chrY (hard-coded, also inside savana to), so chrM and alt, decoy and unplaced contigs are never used. --savana_chromosomes narrows copy-number calling further.

Parameter Description --savana_pb_minsupport Minimum supporting reads for SAVANA to call a variant on PacBio samples (--min_support with --pb). Default = 10 --savana_pb_pon_filter PacBio tumour-only only: remove SAVANA somatic SVs found in the genome's Severus germline SV panel of normals (pon_file), since SAVANA's PacBio classifier has no tumour-only mode and reports nearly every germline SV as somatic. The filtered *.pon_filtered.classified.somatic.vcf goes to VEP, Padfoot and ReConPlot. No effect on ONT, on paired samples, or without a pon_file. Default = true

docs.title: Report Options
docs.text:
Parameter Description --report_gene_panel Gene panel(s) applied when the report opens, as a comma-separated list. Each entry is none (no filtering), a builtin panel name (lymphoid or sarcoma), or a path to a TSV file with a gene column. Default = null, i.e. unfiltered --report_hmf_resource_dir Your own Hartwig (oncoanalyser) resource bundle for the report's HMF driver annotation, in place of the hosted one (GRCh38, lifted over on CHM13), taking every file from its standard layout. Default = the genome's hosted bundle --report_hmf_driver_panel DriverGenePanel.38.tsv; with --report_hmf_ensembl_data_dir, turns on the HMF driver annotation (overrides the bundle's). Default = off --report_hmf_ensembl_data_dir The bundle's common/ensembl_data directory (ensembl_gene_data.csv, ensembl_trans_exon_data.csv); required for the HMF annotation (overrides the bundle's). Default = off --report_hmf_known_fusions known_fusion_data.38.csv: known-fusion matching of the SV calls (optional; overrides the bundle's). Default = off --report_hmf_hotspots KnownHotspots.somatic.38.vcf.gz: hotspot matching of small variants (optional; overrides the bundle's). Default = off --report_hmf_actionable_bed ActionableCodingPanel.38.bed(.gz): a region flag on small variants (optional; absent from bundle v3; overrides the bundle's). Default = off --report_hmf_liftover_chain GRCh38 → CHM13 chain used to lift the HMF resources over on a CHM13 run. Default = the genome's (the T2T consortium's grch38-chm13v2.chain)

The report is rendered by lrsomatic_report from ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report (ghcr.io/ljwharbers/lrsomatic-report-sif under Singularity/Apptainer), pinned to a tag in modules/local/lrsomaticreport/main.nf. Images are built for linux/amd64 only and Conda is not supported for this step; use --skip_report under -profile conda/mamba. Builtin gene panels live in assets/gene_lists/: a TSV dropped there becomes a valid --report_gene_panel value.

Gene panel filtering is a view, not a filter on the data: every builtin panel is embedded in the report and can be ticked or unticked in the browser; --report_gene_panel only decides which are ticked on load. A custom panel is a tab-separated file with a header row and at least a gene column:

gene    panel   note
TP53    mypanel Tumour suppressor
KRAS    mypanel Oncogene

Optional chrom, start and end columns (all three or none, with the reference declared as a # reference: hg38 line or a reference column) switch SV matching from the VEP gene symbol to position, and an optional applies_to column (snv, sv or blank) scopes a gene to one table. See assets/gene_lists/README.md for the full format.

The builtin lymphoid panel was rebuilt in the release that added applies_to: 234 rows scoped per table, where it had 72 genes filtering both. --report_gene_panel lymphoid therefore gives different filtered tables across that change. sarcoma is unchanged.

nextflow run IntGenomicsLab/lrsomatic \
    -profile <docker/singularity> \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results \
    --report_gene_panel /path/to/mypanel.tsv

docs.title: Applying several panels at once
docs.text:
Pass a comma-separated list to open the report with several panels applied. They are unioned: a variant or SV is kept if it hits any of them. Builtin names and custom paths can be mixed freely.

    --report_gene_panel lymphoid,sarcoma
    --report_gene_panel 'lymphoid,/path/to/mypanel.tsv'

With two or more panels active, each panel_hit entry in the SV table gains a trailing [panel] naming which one matched.

An entry containing a / or ending in .tsv is read as a panel file; anything else is a builtin name, so --report_gene_panel mypanel is looked up as a builtin even if a file called mypanel exists.

Checked at launch:

  • none cannot be combined with a real panel.
  • A panel file that does not exist, or a builtin name that is not bundled, is an error.
  • Two panel files sharing a base name cannot be combined; rename one.

docs.title: Embedding every small variant in the HTML
docs.text:
The report's --embed option decides which small-variant rows the HTML table carries: slim (the default) keeps the HTML small on samples with many variants, full embeds every row. The complete table is written beside the HTML as {sample}_small_variants.tsv.gz either way. There is no pipeline parameter for it; pass it through ext.args in a custom config (-c):

process {
    withName: '.*:LRSOMATICREPORT' {
        ext.args = { "--embed full" }
    }
}

This replaces the --gene-panel arguments the pipeline builds from --report_gene_panel, so name the panels in the same string instead: a builtin as --gene-panel 'lymphoid', a panel file given to --report_gene_panel as --gene-panel 'gene_panels/<file name>' (keep --report_gene_panel set, since it is what stages the file). The --hmf-* arguments are built by the module itself, so ext.args does not affect them.

docs.title: HMF driver annotation
docs.text:
The report can apply the Hartwig Medical Foundation driver catalogue used by oncoanalyser: its driver gene panel, known hotspots and known fusions. It is on by default for --genome GRCh38 and --genome CHM13: the pipeline downloads the genome's hosted bundle once per run (HMF_BUNDLE, about 5 MB, MD5-checked), the subset of the oncoanalyser resource bundle v2.2.0 the report reads, already lifted over for CHM13 (see IntGenomicsLab/test-datasets references/hmf/). Turn it off with --skip_report_hmf. Other genomes (including a custom --fasta) have no bundle and render the report without it.

The unpacked bundle is published under <outdir>/cache/hmf/hmf_report_<genome>/ (or --outdir_cache); on an offline host, or to skip the download, give that directory back as --report_hmf_resource_dir.

Your own resources. --report_hmf_resource_dir (a bundle directory) or the individual --report_hmf_* files take over from the hosted bundle, for example a newer oncoanalyser release. Bundles v2.x and v3.x are both read.

    --genome GRCh38 \
    --report_hmf_resource_dir /path/to/hmf_pipeline_resources.38_v2.2.0--3

--report_hmf_resource_dir picks up common/DriverGenePanel.38.tsv, common/ensembl_data/, dna/sv/known_fusion_data.38.csv, dna/variants/KnownHotspots.somatic.38.vcf.gz and, where present, dna/variants/ActionableCodingPanel.38.bed(.gz). Any --report_hmf_* file parameter overrides that one file, and they can be given without a bundle directory. The driver panel and the Ensembl data cache are required (an error at launch otherwise); the other three each switch their part of the section on.

What the report does with them (the report's README has every rule and threshold):

  • Small variants on a panel gene's canonical transcript are reported per the panel's reportMissense / reportNonsense / reportSplice / reportSomaticHotspot flags.
  • Copy number: amplification (minimum CN > 3 × ploidy) and deletion (minimum CN < 0.5) are called from ASCAT and from Wakhan separately, and every deletion called by Severus or SAVANA over a deletion-flagged gene is listed too. Each source can be switched off in the browser.
  • Fusions: Severus and SAVANA breakends are matched to HMF's known pairs, promiscuous partners (with exon ranges), exon deletions/duplications and IG/enhancer regions, with a phase check.
  • The driver panel is also added to the report's gene lists as hmf_driver.

CHM13. The hosted CHM13 bundle is the GRCh38 one lifted over as described here. If you give your own GRCh38 bundle on --genome CHM13, HMF_LIFTOVER lifts it over once per run with --report_hmf_liftover_chain and the CHM13 FASTA, and the report uses the lifted copy. The default chain is the T2T consortium's GRCh38 → T2T-CHM13v2.0 grch38-chm13v2.chain (public domain), downloaded at launch (about 6 MB). On an offline or air-gapped host, download it once and pass its local path with --report_hmf_liftover_chain, or reuse a bundle the pipeline already lifted (below); a chain that cannot be reached is an error at launch.

  • Ensembl data cache: a canonical transcript is kept only if every exon lifts whole, onto one contig and strand, in rank order, its span roughly kept; a gene without one is dropped. With the v2.2.0 bundle that keeps 38,946 of 39,500 transcripts and 528 of the 530 driver genes (OR4F21 and TPTE are dropped).
  • Hotspots: the REF is re-checked on CHM13 (9,302 of 9,305 kept).
  • Actionable panel and IG/enhancer ranges: lifted as regions (all of them with the v2.2.0 bundle); the orientation flips where the chain inverts.
  • Driver panel: copied unchanged.

The lifted copy declares its build (common/ensembl_data/REFERENCE = t2t), counts what was dropped in hmf_liftover_report.tsv, and is published under pipeline_info/hmf_liftover/hmf_chm13/. Giving that directory back as --report_hmf_resource_dir on later CHM13 runs skips the lift. Lifted resources on a GRCh38 run are an error.

On CHM13 the VEP cache's transcript ids are not HMF's Ensembl GRCh38 ones, so the report reads each variant's effect on VEP's canonical transcript (matched to the panel by gene symbol) instead of HMF's canonical transcript. The report's footnote says which rule applied.

It re-implements HMF's reporting rules on the long-read calls; it is not PURPLE or LINX. There is no dNdS driver likelihood, no biallelic or germline reporting and no SV chaining, and ActionableCodingPanel is only a region flag (HMF uses it as a calling-sensitivity tier, not as actionability evidence).

docs.title: WAKHAN Options
docs.text: Parameter Description --wakhan_chroms A string specifying a subset of chromosomes for WAKHAN to process, e.g. "chr1,chr2". Default = null

docs.title: Mutational Signature Options
docs.text:
Mutational signature analysis runs SigProfilerMatrixGenerator on the PASS SNVs and indels of each sample's phased somatic VCF and fits COSMIC signatures per sample with SigProfilerAssignment. It needs SigProfilerMatrixGenerator's per-genome payload (~3 GB), which is not shipped with the pipeline:

  • by default (--download_sigprofiler_genome true) the payload is downloaded during the run, checksum-verified and published to <outdir>/cache/sigprofiler/volume (or <outdir_cache>/sigprofiler/volume with --outdir_cache);
  • --sigprofiler_genome_dir points at an existing SigProfilerMatrixGenerator volume instead (a directory containing tsb/<genome>/, e.g. one created with SigProfilerMatrixGenerator install GRCh38 --volume <dir> or the published cache from a previous run). It takes precedence over the download, so pass it on later runs to skip the ~3 GB fetch.

Running with --download_sigprofiler_genome false and no --sigprofiler_genome_dir, or with a --genome that has no SigProfilerMatrixGenerator genome and no --sigprofiler_genome, stops the pipeline at start-up unless --skip_signatures is set.

A volume passed with --sigprofiler_genome_dir is checked once per run against the chromosome checksums of the pipeline's SigProfilerMatrixGenerator (SIGPROFILER_VERIFY). If a chromosome file is missing or a checksum differs, the run stops before any sample is processed, and the error says which of the two it found. A genome the image has no checksums for is rejected too.

[!WARNING] GRCh38 and CHM13-T2T payloads installed before this release no longer pass that check. SigProfilerMatrixGenerator corrected how both are encoded, and the payloads it now downloads differ from the earlier ones. Reinstall once with --download_sigprofiler_genome, or with SigProfilerMatrixGenerator install <genome> --volume <dir> from the same image, and pass the new volume on later runs. Mutation counts and COSMIC fits are unaffected. Only the strand-split matrices (for example SBS288 and SBS384) change, slightly.

Parameter Description --sigprofiler_genome_dir Full path to a SigProfilerMatrixGenerator volume containing tsb/<sigprofiler_genome>/. Default = null --download_sigprofiler_genome A boolean to download and install the genome payload during the run when no --sigprofiler_genome_dir is given (published to <outdir>/cache/sigprofiler/volume). Default = true --sigprofiler_cosmic_version COSMIC reference signature version fitted by SigProfilerAssignment. Default = 3.6 --sigprofiler_exclude_signature_subgroups Comma-separated SigProfilerAssignment signature subgroups to exclude from the fit, e.g. "Artifact_signatures,Lymphoid_signatures" (see the SigProfilerAssignment documentation). Default = null --sigprofiler_matrix_args Extra arguments for SigProfilerMatrixGenerator matrix_generator; --bed_file, --exome and --seqInfo False are not supported. Default = "--plot" --sigprofiler_assignment_args Extra arguments for SigProfilerAssignment cosmic_fit, e.g. "--make_plots False". Default = null

Both tools run from ghcr.io/ljwharbers/sigprofiler, which adds CHM13 support not yet in a SigProfiler release: SigProfilerMatrixGenerator from the branch behind SigProfilerSuite/SigProfilerMatrixGenerator#250 and SigProfilerAssignment from ljwharbers/SigProfilerAssignment, with COSMIC SBS/DBS signatures renormalised to CHM13. ID83 signatures always use the GRCh37 set. Conda is not supported for this step.

docs.title: Padfoot Options
docs.text:
Padfoot annotates somatic SVs and CNAs with gene/exon overlap, repeat context and complex-SV grouping. It is run for every available SV/CNA caller pair, for paired and tumour-only samples alike:

  • padfoot/severus_wakhan/ -- Severus somatic SVs + the top-ranked Wakhan solution's integer copy-number profile (solution_rank_1/integer_profile.vcf; requires Wakhan not skipped)
  • padfoot/savana/ -- SAVANA classified somatic SVs + SAVANA segmented absolute copy number (requires SAVANA CNA, i.e. an SNP source: the phased germline VCF for paired samples, or the bundled 1000G panel for tumour-only samples on GRCh38/CHM13). Samples without SAVANA CNA are silently skipped.

Padfoot is not distributed on bioconda. The module's image (docker.io/timmy9527/padfoot-repeatmasker, recipe in containers/padfoot/) ships a pinned commit of the Tim-Yu/Padfoot fork, which adds SAVANA input support (to be proposed upstream), so nothing is downloaded at run time. Padfoot is therefore not available under -profile conda: use Docker, Singularity or Apptainer, or --skip_padfoot.

RepeatMasker (used only to classify the sequence of novel insertions) runs by default; the image ships the Dfam 4.0 root and curated-consensus partitions. --padfoot_run_repeatmasker false skips it.

Gene copy number in by_gene.tsv is labelled against the tumour ploidy: the module passes the CN caller's fitted purity/ploidy table (Wakhan solutions_ranks.tsv, SAVANA *_fitted_purity_ploidy.tsv) and Padfoot compares each haplotype's integer copy number with ploidy/2 (SAVANA's fractional major/minor copy numbers are rounded first). Without a fit table Padfoot estimates the ploidy from the profile and says so in padfoot.log; segments without a minor-allele estimate are reported as NA.

Padfoot bundles gene and repeat annotations for hg38 and mm10 only. For other genomes (e.g. CHM13) provide --padfoot_gff (a GENCODE-style GFF3, plain or gzipped) and --padfoot_rm (a RepeatMasker .out, or a BED of chromosome, start, end and repeat class), both on the same assembly as --genome; otherwise Padfoot is skipped with a warning. --padfoot_genome must match --genome (hg38 annotations on CHM13 coordinates would be wrong), so a mismatch stops the run at start-up.

Parameter Description --padfoot_genome Padfoot genome preset (hg38, chm13, mm10). Default = null (inferred from --genome) --padfoot_gff Custom GFF3 gene annotation. Default = null (bundled) --padfoot_rm Custom RepeatMasker annotation. Default = null (bundled) --padfoot_run_repeatmasker Run RepeatMasker on inserted sequences (repeat class of novel insertions); the image ships the Dfam 4.0 root and curated-consensus partitions. Default = true

docs.title: ReConPlot Options
docs.text:
ReConPlot rearrangement + copy-number figures are generated through the wrapper shipped in assets/reconplot/ (vendored from Tim-Yu/ReConPlot) for every CN/SV caller pair available for a sample, into reconplot/<pair>/: The ReConPlot R package (not on conda) ships inside the module's image (docker.io/timmy9527/reconplot, recipe in containers/reconplot/), so nothing is downloaded at run time and the module is not available under -profile conda.

  • severus_ascat/ -- ASCAT allele-specific CN + Severus somatic SVs
  • severus_wakhan/ -- Wakhan top-ranked solution CN (solution_rank_1/integer_profile.bed) + Severus somatic SVs
  • savana/ -- SAVANA absolute CN + SAVANA classified somatic SVs (read from *.classified.somatic.vcf, which SAVANA writes on every platform; its somatic BEDPE comes from the ONT classifier only)

Each pair produces per_chromosome/ (one figure per chromosome), genome_wide/ (all chromosomes in one strip), the harmonised CN/SV tables, and, when --reconplot_regions is set, a focus/ multi-panel figure with optional gene labels and BAF track.

Parameter Description --reconplot_genome ReConPlot genome preset (hg38, hg19, T2T, mm10, mm39). Default = null (inferred from --genome) --reconplot_max_cn Copy-number axis ceiling. Default = 8 --reconplot_min_svlen Drop intra-chromosomal SVs shorter than this (bp); translocations kept. Default = 0 --reconplot_max_svs Draw at most this many SVs, the best supported first, in each of the per-chromosome set (one budget shared by all chromosome figures), the genome-wide strip and the focus panel; a figure missing some of its SVs says top N of M SVs in its title, and the *.reconplot_sv.tsv table keeps every SV. 0 = no limit. Default = 1000 --reconplot_exclude_vntr Drop Severus SVs flagged inside a VNTR. Default = false --reconplot_regions Regions for an extra focus/ panel, e.g. "chr8,chr17:30000000-50000000" (syntax checked at start-up; regions on contigs without copy-number data are skipped with a warning, and no focus panel is produced if none is left). Default = null (no focus panel) --reconplot_genes Comma-separated HUGO symbols labelled on the focus panel. Default = null --reconplot_baf_track Add a het-SNP BAF track to the focus panel (ASCAT and SAVANA only). Default = false --reconplot_format Output formats: pdf, png or pdf,png. Default = pdf,png

docs.title: ShatterSeek Options
docs.text:
ShatterSeek chromothripsis calls are made for every CN/SV caller pair available for a sample (severus_ascat, severus_wakhan, savana, the same pairs as ReConPlot), into shatterseek/<pair>/, and each chromosome's cluster is labelled with the PCAWG high-confidence tiers (see output). The pipeline runs upstream ShatterSeek with a build-time patch adding T2T-CHM13; it ships inside the module's image (oras://docker.io/robertaforsyth/shatterseek-sif under Singularity/Apptainer, docker.io/robertaforsyth/shatterseek otherwise, recipe in containers/shatterseek/), so the module is not available under -profile conda. The callers are read by the same parsers as ReConPlot (assets/reconplot/R/parsers), through the wrapper in assets/shatterseek/.

Parameter Description --shatterseek_genome ShatterSeek genome (hg38, chm13, hg19). Default = null (inferred from --genome; skipped with a warning otherwise) --shatterseek_min_svlen Drop intra-chromosomal SVs shorter than this (bp) before ShatterSeek; translocations kept. Default = 150

Tier cut-offs (--min-sv-hc1, --min-osc-hc, --min-sv-hc2, --min-tra-hc2, --min-sv-hc3, --no-hc3), the significance level (--alpha, default 0.2), q-values or raw P values (--use q|p) and the other SV filters (--min-support, --exclude-vntr) are wrapper options, set through ext.args (keep --min-svlen in it, or use --shatterseek_min_svlen, since ext.args replaces the pipeline's value):

process {
    withName: '.*:SHATTERSEEK_(SEVERUS_ASCAT|SEVERUS_WAKHAN|SAVANA)' { ext.args = '--min-svlen 150 --no-hc3' }
}

docs.title: Offline and air-gapped systems
docs.text:
Both modules use the same pinned-tag pair as the pipeline's other large custom images (ClairS-TO): a prebuilt SIF (oras://docker.io/timmy9527/<name>-sif:<tag>) under Singularity/Apptainer and the Docker image (docker.io/timmy9527/<name>:<tag>) otherwise, both on Docker Hub, so nf-core pipelines download --container-system singularity stages them like every other container in the pipeline. To use a different image (e.g. a local mirror) override it in a config file:

process {
    withName: '.*:PADFOOT_(SEVERUS_WAKHAN|SAVANA)' { container = '/path/to/padfoot-repeatmasker.sif' }
    withName: '.*:RECONPLOT_(SEVERUS_ASCAT|SEVERUS_WAKHAN|SAVANA)' { container = '/path/to/reconplot.sif' }
    withName: '.*:SHATTERSEEK_(SEVERUS_ASCAT|SEVERUS_WAKHAN|SAVANA)' { container = '/path/to/shatterseek.sif' }
}

Neither step downloads anything at run time: Padfoot and the ReConPlot R package are inside the two images, and the ReConPlot wrapper is part of the pipeline. Updating either tool means rebuilding its image, pushing the Docker image and its SIF twin, and bumping the tags in the module (see the READMEs under containers/).

docs.title: Variant Filtering and Combining Options
docs.text:
These options control how variants from multiple callers are filtered and merged.

Parameter Description --germline_var_keep Comma-separated germline callers to run: deepvariant, clair. Default = clair --somatic_var_keep Comma-separated somatic callers to run: deepsomatic, clair. Default = clair --germline_var_combine How to combine germline caller outputs: consensus (shared calls only) or all (union). Default = all --somatic_var_combine How to combine somatic caller outputs: consensus (shared calls only) or all (union). Default = all --prioritize_caller_germline Whose record to use where both germline callers call a variant: deepvariant or clair. Default = clair --prioritize_caller_somatic Whose record to use where both somatic callers call a variant: deepsomatic or clair. Default = clair --smallvar_filter_pass Keep only PASS records from each small variant caller downstream (the tumour-only ClairS-TO somatic split is PASS-only either way, see below). Default = true

DeepVariant and DeepSomatic emit a record for every site they evaluate, not only for the variants they call, so most of their records are RefCall, GERMLINE or PON; Clair3 and ClairS also keep their LowQual and NonSomatic records. Without a PASS filter, *_var_combine = 'all' would carry all of these into the phased VCFs and the mutation burden.

--smallvar_filter_pass (true by default) restricts the copy of each caller's VCF that is handed to the caller consensus, phasing, VEP and the report. In tumor-only mode VCFSPLIT always restricts ClairS-TO's somatic split to PASS. Its germline split takes the NonSomatic calls and those Verdict tagged Verdict_Germline; with the filter on, a NonSomatic call is kept only if NonSomatic is its sole FILTER (a LowQual;NonSomatic call is dropped), while Verdict's germline calls are kept although Verdict marks them LowQual. The germline split is then PASS-rewritten, with the original value kept in INFO/ORIG_FILTER. The tumour-only DeepVariant germline arm is PASS-only whatever the setting: a PASS filter runs before the DeepSomatic verdict selection, so RefCall records never enter it. The per-caller VCFs published under <outdir>/<sample>/variants/<caller> are never filtered, so no calls are lost from the results directory.

Set it to false to pass on non-PASS calls as well, with their original FILTER: Clair3 and ClairS records as they are (LowQual included), and DeepVariant and DeepSomatic records whose genotype carries an alternate allele and whose FILTER is PASS or LowQual. DeepVariant and DeepSomatic records without a call (RefCall, NoCall; over 40 million on a 30x genome with DeepSomatic) are never passed on, nor are DeepSomatic's GERMLINE records (written as 0/0) and PON records: like ClairS-TO's NonSomatic calls, they are its verdict that a site is not somatic. The two tumour-only germline arms above stay PASS-only, and the ClairS-TO germline split is still PASS-rewritten. The tumour-only ClairS-TO somatic split also stays PASS-only, so its LowQual somatic candidates are dropped whatever the setting, while paired ClairS passes its LowQual calls on with false.

DeepSomatic 1.10 declares FORMAT/NAF as Number=R but writes one value per alternate allele. Before its records reach any step that joins records (bcftools norm -m +any), the pipeline declares the field Number=A in its working copy (DEEPSOMATIC_PASS_FILTER); the published DeepSomatic VCF keeps the caller's header.

consensus keeps the prioritised caller's records whose called alleles are all called by the other caller too. An allele counts as called when the record's genotype carries it, not merely when it is listed in ALT, and alleles are matched on CHROM, POS, REF and ALT after splitting and left-aligning, so a multi-allelic record can match the other caller's biallelic ones. The record is published as the prioritised caller wrote it, with its own genotype and all its ALT alleles, so no genotype is made up. Where the callers disagree on the genotype of a shared allele (e.g. 1/1 against 0/1), the prioritised caller's genotype is kept. A record is left out when:

  • none of its called alleles is called by the other caller, for example DeepVariant C>A,G 2/2 against Clair3 C>A 0/1 (A is listed by DeepVariant but not called);
  • only some of its called alleles are shared, for example DeepVariant A>G,T 1/2 against Clair3 A>G 1/1: the T allele has only one caller's support, so the site is not a consensus call;
  • its genotype carries no alternate allele (0/0, ./.).

Earlier versions rejoined the split alleles after the intersection instead, which published records such as C>A 0/0 or A>G 1/0 that neither caller had called.

all keeps the union by position, one caller per position: the prioritised caller's records, plus the other caller's records at positions where the prioritised caller has none. Where both callers call a position, even with different alleles, only the prioritised caller's records are kept. A PASS record wins over a non-PASS one first, so with --smallvar_filter_pass false the prioritised caller's LowQual record does not hide the other caller's PASS call, and a caller's non-PASS record at a position where it has a PASS one is dropped. Where one caller reports several different alleles at one position (e.g. Clair3 calls an SNV and a deletion starting at the same base), all of them are kept; only exact duplicates (same POS, REF and ALT) are dropped. Records are not split in this mode.

Whatever the callers and combine mode, the germline set is joined to one record per position (bcftools norm -m +any) before phasing, since LongPhase cannot take two records at one POS. The somatic set keeps the callers' records.

docs.title: Somatic phasing
docs.text:
LongPhase phases the germline variants (on the normal, or on the tumour without one), and every BAM is haplotagged from that phased germline VCF. Somatic variants are then phased from the haplotagged tumour reads, so their haplotype and phase set agree with the germline VCF and with the HP/PS read tags:

  • For each heterozygous somatic SNV, deletion or insertion, the reads carrying the ALT allele are counted per haplotype (HP) and phase block (PS). Only ALT reads count: reference reads come from both haplotypes and from normal cells, so they say nothing about where the mutation sits.
  • With at least 3 tagged ALT reads, of which at least 80 % share one HP and PS, the record gets GT 1|0 (HP 1) or 0|1 (HP 2) and that PS, the germline block's ID.
  • Tumour-only samples also need at least 3 tagged reads (any allele) on the other haplotype of that phase block at the site. Without a normal, the germline phase is built from tumour reads, and in some regions haplotagging puts reads of both haplotypes on one HP. A site where every read carries the same HP is then no evidence, and phasing it would be close to a coin flip. Paired samples are haplotagged from the normal's phase, so a site with all tumour reads on one haplotype (loss of heterozygosity) is phased as usual.
  • Otherwise the record is left unphased, as are homozygous, multi-allelic, complex and 0/0/./. records. No record is removed.
  • FORMAT/AHP gives the ALT reads on haplotype 1, on haplotype 2 and without a haplotag, and FORMAT/OHP the tagged reads on the other haplotype, so an unphased record shows why (no tagged reads, reads split across the haplotypes, or no reads on the other haplotype).

docs.title: PON Options
docs.text: Parameter Description --clairsto_pon_vcfs Full path to one or more Panel of Normals VCF files for ClairS-TO small variant filtering. Default = null, meaning the set for --genome is used: four VCFs on GRCh38, five on CHM13. Supplying VCFs replaces that set entirely rather than adding to it --clairsto_pon_flags Population allele matching flags for ClairS-TO PON VCFs (one per VCF, comma-separated). Default = null, meaning the flags that go with the --genome set. There must be exactly one flag per VCF, or the run stops at startup --deepsomatic_pon_vcfs Full path to one or more bgzipped, tabix-indexed PON VCF files (for example, .vcf.gz) passed to DeepSomatic --population_vcfs. If not set, uses container-bundled defaults in tumor-only mode or no PON in paired mode. Default = null

docs.title: Advanced Options
docs.text: Parameter Description --use_gpu A boolean to run the GPU-capable steps on a GPU, with their GPU container images: DeepVariant and DeepSomatic call_variants (DEEPVARIANT_CALLVARIANTS, DEEPSOMATIC_CALLVARIANTS; their make_examples step uses the same -gpu image but stays on the CPU) and Clair3 (CLAIR3). Every other step, including the fibertools-rs steps (m6A prediction, nucleosomes, FIRE), runs on the CPU either way. Needs a GPU-enabled compute environment; add the gpu profile (-profile <...>,gpu) so the containers can see the GPU. The DeepVariant/DeepSomatic 1.10.0-gpu images (TensorFlow 2.16.1, CUDA 12.3) and Clair3's GPU image (hkubal/clair3:v2.0.5_gpu) support NVIDIA GPUs up to the Hopper generation (compute capability 9.0 or lower, for example A100, H100 or RTX Ada). On Blackwell cards such as the B200 (compute capability 10.0) call_variants fails with CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PTX and Clair3 fails too; there, leave --use_gpu off. Default = false --generate_gvcf A boolean to enable gVCF output from DeepVariant (germline) and DeepSomatic (somatic). gVCF files include calls at all positions, not just variant sites. Default = false
